Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal (increase/maintain/decrease) of unpleasant pictures in human older adults and reports task-related BOLD activation in medial prefrontal regions and amygdala. No exclusion criteria are met. Satisfies inclusion criteria I1–I4; include for full-text review.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study with task-related anterior insula activation during aversive anticipation (I1, I4) in human participants (I3). It is unclear whether participants performed an instructed emotion regulation task (I2) because effects relate to dispositional reappraisal rather than instructed regulation. Inclusion status is uncertain from abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

Study is a task-based fMRI of human participants reporting task-related activation/connectivity, but participants were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses. It examines pharmacological effects during virtual aggression rather than an emotion-regulation task, so I2 is not met. No exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI with human participants (n=10) instructed to decrease emotional reactions (emotion regulation) vs passive viewing; reports task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria met.

Study is a resting-state arterial spin labeling test-retest reliability study, not a task-based fMRI emotion regulation experiment. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (healthy human participants). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

EXCLUDED: Study used resting-state fMRI (not task-based) and did not include an emotion-regulation task or report task-related activation results. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results). No exclusion criteria were met (exclusion_criteria_applied = []).

This is a task-based fMRI study (I1) with human participants (I3) reporting task-related activations (I4), but it does not involve an emotion-regulation task of emotional visual stimuli or instructions to regulate emotional responses (I2 not met).

Task-based fMRI in human participants (N=24) instructed to view or decrease emotional responses to pictured stimuli (emotion regulation). Reports task-related brain activation. No exclusion criteria met (not a review/meta-analysis, not an empathy/perspective-taking study without regulation instruction).

Excluded: study used gratitude meditation/resting-state and functional connectivity analyses rather than a task-based emotion-regulation paradigm with emotional visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task as defined), I4 (task-related brain activation results). Exclusion criteria met: none.

EXCLUDED because the study does not address emotion regulation of visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related brain activation). Inclusion criterion not met/not demonstrated: I2 (emotion regulation task) — study examines intrinsic motivation and responses to errors/reward, not regulation of emotional responses. No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) apply.

No exclusion criteria met. The study is a task-based fMRI study (I1), uses human participants (I3), and reports task-related brain activation results (I4). However participants viewed emotional scenes after a depletion manipulation and were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses; thus I2 (an emotion regulation task) is not demonstrated. Therefore exclude based on failure to meet I2.

No exclusion criteria met (E1/E2: none). Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met / not demonstrated: I2 — the study examines pain processing/meditation during thermal stimulation, not regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli as specified by the review objective. Therefore excluded for not addressing the review objective.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human patient sample). Inclusion criteria NOT met or not demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study — focuses on white matter network/structural connectivity), I2 (no emotion regulation task reported), I4 (no task-related brain activation results reported). Therefore study is excluded from this meta-analysis.

Task-based fMRI with human participants and task-related activation reported (I1, I3, I4). Abstract does not indicate an explicit emotion-regulation instruction or strategy (I2 unclear); study examines individual differences in external motivation during face evaluation. No exclusion criteria clearly met. Include for full-text review to determine whether an emotion-regulation task was used.

E2 met: participants judged another's affect (perspective-taking/empathy) with no instruction to amplify/dampen their own emotions. Inclusion: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human older adult sample), I4 (reports task-related brain activation) are satisfied. Inclusion I2 is not demonstrated (no emotion-regulation instructions reported).

No task-based emotion regulation paradigm reported: study uses resting-state fMRI examining inflammation and rsFC. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants implied). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not task-based fMRI), I2 (no emotion regulation task), I4 (no task-related activation reported).

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I1), an implicit emotion-regulation/emotion-label task (I2), human adolescent participants (I3), and reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results (I4). No exclusion criteria met.

FMRI component (Study 2) involved recalling negative autobiographical memories rather than regulating emotional responses to visual stimuli targeted by the meta-analysis objective. Inclusion met: I1, I2, I3, I4. Inclusion not demonstrated: fMRI regulation of responses to visual stimuli (meta-analysis target). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI paradigm of face emotional processing with ICA showing components modulated by fear and possible implicit reappraisal, but does not state whether participants were instructed to regulate emotions or explicitly that subjects were human; insufficient detail to determine I2/I3—include for full-text review.

Abstract is truncated and provides insufficient information to determine whether participants performed an emotion-regulation task (I2). Title indicates a human task-based fMRI fear-conditioning study reporting BOLD results in vmPFC, satisfying I1, I3, and I4. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to assess whether emotion regulation instructions were used.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I2, I3, I4. NOT eligible for this meta-analysis because it does not address the review objective requiring regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli: emotion was regulated for internally generated autobiographical memories (non-visual), so the study does not match the stimulus modality required by the review.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of attentional deployment as an emotion regulation strategy (regulate vs natural viewing) in human participants, reporting task-related neural activation and connectivity results; no exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study using a film-based emotion regulation task in human adolescents/young adults and presents task-related neural activation results (prefrontal cortex, amygdala). No exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI not stated in abstract), I2 (classical conditioning/nocebo paradigm is not an explicit emotion-regulation task), I4 (no report of task-related brain activation results in abstract). I3 (human participants) is not explicitly stated. Abstract lacks evidence of the required emotion-regulation fMRI paradigm, so exclude.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) using standardized negative scripts in human participants, with clinical and control groups and task-related brain activation results. All inclusion criteria are met; include for full-text review to confirm stimulus modality (script-driven vs. visual) and extract activation contrasts.

Task-based fMRI with human offender participants who were instructed to actively modulate (increase) their level of concern for people in pain (an emotion-regulation instruction). The study reports task-related neural activation changes, satisfying inclusion criteria I1–I4. No exclusion criteria are met (E2 not applicable because participants were explicitly instructed to amplify their emotional response).

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (preliminary task-based fMRI reported), I3 (human clinical and control groups), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (no emotion-regulation task; study uses monetary decision-making assessing risk/loss aversion, not instructed regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli).

Task-based fMRI study (I1) with children and adults viewing emotional video clips and reporting task-related brain activation results (I4). Participant sample qualifies (I3). The abstract does not state an explicit emotion-regulation instruction (I2 not demonstrated), but the review objective allows passive viewing; include for full-text review to confirm applicability.

Task-based fMRI with human participants performing affect labeling, an incidental emotion-regulation strategy; reports task-related brain activation and modulatory effects (amygdala dampening). Meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are indicated in the abstract.

Task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal in healthy human participants; reports task-related brain activation (amygdala attenuation and amygdala–prefrontal connectivity). No exclusion criteria met (not a review and not an empathy/perspective-taking study without regulation instructions).

Abstract describes analysis of multi-subject fMRI data with stimuli and mentions application to an emotion regulation study; exclusion criteria not met. Abstract lacks sufficient detail to confirm that participants performed an emotion-regulation task or that task-related activation results are reported, so include for full-text review.

Excluded because the laboratory task was a dot-probe attentional threat task, not an instructed emotion-regulation task. No exclusion criteria apply. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (clinical youth sample), I4 (reports task-related neural connectivity/activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (no emotion regulation instructions/strategy during the fMRI task).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study of human participants using voluntary suppression of negative affect (an emotion regulation strategy) and examining neural substrates, reporting task-related brain activation results. This meets I1–I4 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in humans examining neural responses during passive viewing and effortful emotion regulation of positive and negative stimuli following child maltreatment, and reports neural response findings. This meets I1, I2, I3, and I4; no exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract.

Abstract reports an empirical task-based fMRI study in children performing emotion regulation while viewing emotionally expressive faces and reports task-related ACC activation patterns. This meets inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria apply.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I1 (task-based event-related fMRI), I3 (healthy human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I2 (this study manipulated attention to emotional stimuli via rTMS and cueing but did not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses).

Abstract reports task-based fMRI with behavioral and fMRI measures, describes transfer to an emotion regulation measure, and links regulation gains to task-related brain activation. Human participants are implied. Thus it meets I1–I4 and no exclusion criteria are evident.

Abstract indicates neuroimaging of emotion regulation circuitry in symptomatic youth but does not explicitly state a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation task or report task-related activation. Insufficient information to confirm I1, I2, and I4 from abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants - sample of 1106 adults). Inclusion criteria NOT met / not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation results). This is a structural MRI study of cortical surface area and amygdala volume related to trait neuroticism, not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study.

Task-based fMRI with human participants performing explicit and implicit emotional suppression (an emotion regulation task) while viewing negative/neutral images; reports task-related neural activation and connectivity. No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to confirm details.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in human young adults and task-related brain activation (I1, I3, I4). However, it does not state participants were instructed to regulate their emotions or perform an emotion-regulation strategy (I2 not demonstrated). Inclusion for full-text review is warranted to determine whether an emotion-regulation component was present.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI experiment (I1) with human participants (I3) asked to suppress thoughts about negative relationship scenarios—an emotion-regulation strategy (I2)—and reports task-related brain activation results (I4). The abstract does not state whether stimuli were visual (meta-analysis focuses on visual-stimulus regulation), so suitability for that narrower objective is uncertain; include for full-text review.

Excluded because I2 is not met: the study manipulated ketamine during memory encoding of emotional pictures but did not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related brain activation reported). No exclusion criteria (E1/E2) are met.

The study uses task-based fMRI in humans and reports task-related activations (I1, I3, I4). However, it does not investigate emotion regulation of emotional visual stimuli nor instruct participants to change/amplify/dampen their emotional responses (I2 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria apply.

No fMRI or emotion-regulation task reported. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human pediatric participants). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants: African American youths followed into adulthood). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation). Study reports resting-state functional connectivity, not a task-based emotion regulation fMRI study.

Participants were passively exposed to infant cry sounds; no emotion regulation instructions or task are described (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activation). Exclusion criteria met: none (E1,E2 not applicable).

E2 applies — this is an empathy/perspective-taking fMRI study where participants viewed others' pain without being instructed to regulate (amplify/dampen) their emotional responses. Inclusion I1, I3, I4 are met; I2 is not met/not demonstrated (no emotion-regulation task reported).

Abstract indicates study examines emotion regulatory brain function in clinical anxiety and depression but provides no methodological details. It does not confirm task-based fMRI, an emotion regulation task, or reporting of task-related brain activation. Include for full-text review to determine whether I1, I2, and I4 are met.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related brain activation reported). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I2 — not an emotion-regulation task and stimuli are auditory (infant laughter), whereas the meta-analysis targets regulation or passive viewing of visual stimuli. Thus study does not address the review objective.

EXCLUDED because inclusion criterion I2 is not met: participants passively viewed emotional pictures and were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human adult participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met. The abstract provides no evidence of an emotion-regulation task.

Abstract reports a task-based whole-brain fMRI study with 55 healthy human participants performing instructed regulation of negative emotion (and viewing without regulating). Task-related activation results are reported (GLM contrasts and task-rest interactions). No exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI in humans viewing emotional pictures (viewing without regulating is allowed by the review objective). Reports task-related brain activation (amygdala reactivity and amygdala–VMPFC connectivity), involves healthy adult participants, and meets inclusions. No exclusion criteria evident from abstract.

Task-based fMRI with 21 healthy human participants performing emotion regulation strategies (mindfulness and suppression) in response to emotional visual stimuli; reports task-related brain activation results (amygdala attenuation and connectivity). Satisfies all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI study reporting cognitive emotion regulation (reappraisal) during scanning in human participants (female sample) with task-related brain activation results (amygdala and prefrontal coupling). No exclusion criteria met and all inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This is a resting-state functional connectivity study, not a task-based fMRI investigation of emotion regulation. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants with patient and control groups). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results).

Task-based fMRI with human participants and task-related activation reported (I1, I3, I4). Abstract does not clearly state that participants were instructed to regulate emotion (I2 not demonstrated), but the study may still be eligible for review because the meta-analysis accepts viewing without explicit regulation. Full-text needed to confirm whether an emotion-regulation instruction or relevant regulation-related paradigm was used.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment in humans that reports task-related brain activation (I1, I3, I4 satisfied). However, the abstract does not clearly state that participants were instructed to perform an emotion regulation task (I2 is uncertain)—while acceptance of unfair offers is discussed as involving regulatory processes, explicit regulation instructions are not described. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to determine I2.

Excluding because the study used a reactive aggression provocation/retaliation task without instructing participants to regulate their emotional responses, so it does not meet I2. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (emotion regulation task not demonstrated). Exclusion criteria met: none.

E2: The study is an fMRI moral-decision and perspective-taking experiment where participants were humanized via implicit mentalizing primes but were not instructed to amplify or dampen their emotional responses (no emotion-regulation instructions). Inclusion met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion not met: I2 (emotion regulation task not demonstrated).

Abstract reports task-based fMRI with human participants and task-related activation (I1, I3, I4). However it does not describe an emotion-regulation task or instructions to regulate emotions; it examines trait attentional control during viewing of social rejection scenes, so I2 is not met. No exclusion criteria clearly apply.

Task-based fMRI in healthy adults reporting task-related brain activation. Abstract does not clearly indicate an instructed emotion-regulation task (primes implicitly modulate regulation), so I2 is uncertain; include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human healthy participants). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion-regulation task), I4 (task-related activation results). Abstract reports structural and resting-state imaging and affect associations but no task-based emotion-regulation fMRI or task activation, so exclude.

Task-based fMRI study of human participants undergoing a social rejection paradigm reporting task-related brain activation. Abstract does not state an explicit emotion-regulation instruction (uncertain if fits I2), so include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Excluded because the study reports task-based fMRI in human participants with task-related activation (I1, I3, I4 met), but the task is associative emotional learning, not an emotion-regulation task or instruction, so I2 is not met. No exclusion criteria are met.

EXCLUDED. No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (not an emotion-regulation task—participants performed prosody categorization/processing, not instructed to regulate emotion). Also does not address review objective of visual-stimulus emotion regulation (auditory speech prosody used).

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI retinotopic mapping), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain mapping results). Inclusion IDs not met: I2 (no emotion regulation task—participants did not regulate emotional responses; study focused on visual field mapping and resting-state connectivity). No evidence of emotion regulation or related task activations; therefore excluded.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of volitional regulation of desire for food (an emotion/craving regulation task) in human participants and examines hemodynamic responses (brain activation). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text should be reviewed to confirm stimulus modality (likely visual) and task details.

Study used resting-state fMRI and diffusion (TBSS) in late-life depression with no task or task-based activation reported. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical group with separate healthy controls). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

Abstract describes an empirical task-based fMRI study of human youth performing an emotional conflict (automatic emotion regulation) task and reports task-related neural activation results (PFC, amygdala, cingulate). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task: focusing away from emotion), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Not suitable for this meta-analysis because the emotional stimuli were internally generated autobiographical memories (not visual stimuli) and thus do not address the review objective of regulation of responses to visual stimuli.

Resting-state fMRI study with no task-based emotion regulation; reports associations between spontaneous activity and resilience/well-being rather than task-related activation. No exclusion criteria met.

Study uses resting-state fMRI (connectivity) rather than a task-based emotion-regulation or viewing task. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion-regulation task), I4 (task-related activation).

Exclusion E2 met: this is an empathy/viewing fMRI study without instructions to amplify or dampen emotion (no regulation task). Inclusion I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), and I4 (task-related brain activation/connectivity results) are satisfied. Inclusion I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task) is not demonstrated in the abstract.

No emotion-regulation instruction reported. Study is a task-based fMRI with children and reports task-related activation (I1, I3, I4 met) but participants viewed emotional faces within a flanker task without regulating them, so I2 is not met. No exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract reports an event-related fMRI task (I1) in which human participants were instructed to increase, decrease, or not alter emotional responses to visual (positive/negative/neutral) pictures—i.e. cognitive emotion regulation (I2). Participants are human (I3) and the paper reports task-related brain activation results (prefrontal, amygdala) (I4). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review.

No task-based fMRI or emotion regulation task reported. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). The study reports resting cerebral blood flow and HF-HRV correlations, not task-related fMRI activation during emotion regulation.

This paper is a meta-analysis (no original human fMRI data) so it meets exclusion E1. Inclusion criteria are not satisfied: it is not a primary task-based fMRI study (I1 not met), does not present original human emotion-regulation task data (I2 not met), does not report original participant groups (I3 not met), and does not report original task-related activation results (I4 not met).

Exclusion: no exclusion criteria met. Inclusion: I3 met (human participants - girls). Inclusion not met: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study; uses diffusion MRI/WM microstructure), I2 (no emotion regulation task; study examines pubertal development), I4 (does not report task-related brain activation). Therefore excluded.

Abstract reports deep (semantic elaboration) vs shallow perceptual viewing of emotional pictures but does not indicate participants were instructed to regulate (reappraise, suppress, or otherwise modulate) their emotional responses. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants, young and older adults), I4 (task-related activation results). Inclusion not met: I2 (emotion regulation task) is not demonstrated in the abstract.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I1 (task-based fMRI: scanned retrieval session with neural recruitment), I3 (human participants across ages), I4 (reports task-related brain activation/connectivity). Not satisfied: I2 — participants performed memory retrieval and vividness ratings but were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses; no emotion-regulation task is described in the abstract.

Abstract reports human participants and neural activation in a task paradigm but does not clearly state use of fMRI (I1) or that the task is an emotion-regulation instruction (I2). Insufficient information to confirm these inclusion criteria; full-text review needed to verify imaging modality and whether the task fits the review’s definition of regulation.

Study examines intrinsic brain activity/connectivity (resting-state) in obesity, not a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

Study used auditory emotional stimuli (sounds), not visual stimuli, so it does not address the review objective. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I1, I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I2 (uncertain whether compassion meditation here counts as an emotion regulation task).

Task-based fMRI with human participants instructed to cognitively regulate responses to visual food stimuli (control urge to eat vs imagine consumption); reports task-related brain activation results in prefrontal and precuneus regions; meets I1, I2, I3, I4. No exclusion criteria met.

Excluded because the study examines regulation of pain (somatosensory) rather than regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli required by the review objective. Abstract meets I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation/anticipation/acceptance), I3 (human participants), and I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria (E1,E2) apply. However, it does not address emotional regulation of visual stimuli, so it falls outside the meta-analysis objective.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in humans using cognitive reappraisal to regulate craving (an emotion regulation task), with reported task-related brain activation results. All inclusion criteria (I1–I4) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Include for full-text review.

Excluded because the study used resting-state fMRI (no task) and examined functional connectivity related to neuropsychiatric symptoms in Parkinson’s disease; it does not meet I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), or I4 (task-related activation results). No exclusion criteria were met.

Abstract provides no evidence of a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm; appears to report DNA methylation and functional network architecture (likely resting-state or molecular imaging). Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I3 (human participants not confirmed in abstract), I4 (task-related activation results).

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none (no evidence in abstract). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (study is resting-state fMRI, not task-based), I2 (does not involve an emotion regulation task or viewing/regulating emotional visual stimuli), I4 (no task-related activation reported). I3 (participant type not clearly demonstrated in abstract). Therefore excluded.

Exclusion based on abstract: No task-based fMRI data or reported task-related brain activation (I1 and I4 not met). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1, I4.

This study used a self-retrieval/self-reflection paradigm (self, ideal, avatar) rather than an instructed emotion-regulation task (e.g., reappraisal, distancing) for visual emotional stimuli. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human clinical and control groups), I4 (reports task-related activations). Inclusion not met: I2 (no evidence of emotion-regulation instructions). No exclusion criteria clearly met (E2 not clearly applicable).

Study uses EEG/ERP, not fMRI, so I1 is not met; the task is an emotion-word Stroop (emotional interference), not an emotion regulation task, so I2 is not met. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants) and I4 (reports task-related brain activation via ERPs). No exclusion criteria met. Abstract clearly describes ERP methods rather than fMRI; therefore excluded.

Task-based fMRI with human participants performing voluntary emotion regulation (attentional deployment) during anticipation of bivalent visual/auditory stimuli; reports task-related activation results (ventral striatum, insula, vmPFC, PCC). Meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are indicated from the abstract.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Study used resting-state fMRI after intranasal oxytocin and reports resting-state connectivity, not task activation or emotion regulation.

EXCLUDED: Study is resting-state fMRI examining amygdala functional connectivity in children and genetic/stress predictors, not a task-based emotion regulation fMRI. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants, children). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation results).

EXCLUDED: study uses diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), not task-based fMRI; no emotion-regulation task or task-related activation reported. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human clinical pediatric sample). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results). Abstract describes clinical neurosurgical outcomes for pediatric thalamic tumors, not an emotion-regulation task fMRI study; therefore excluded.

Task-based fMRI with human participants performing implicit emotion regulation (attention shifting and appraisal). Reports task-related brain activation in adults followed from childhood, matching the review objective and meeting inclusion criteria I1–I4. No exclusion criteria met.

The study reports a task-based fMRI emotional face processing task in healthy adults and presents task-related activation/connectivity results (I1, I3, I4). The abstract does not specify an emotion-regulation instruction (I2 is unclear), but the review accepts studies that view emotional stimuli without regulating; therefore include for full-text review to resolve this. No exclusion criteria met.

Excluded because the study did not use task-based fMRI (I1 not met); it used magnetoencephalography and structural MRI. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (task involving inhibition of aversive socio-emotional stimuli), I3 (human participants—school-age children), I4 (reports task-related functional brain activity). Exclusion criteria met: none.

No emotion-regulation task is described in the abstract: it examines audiovisual emotional congruence (music + faces) rather than instructed regulation of participants' emotional responses. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related activation). Inclusion not met: I2 (emotion regulation task not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are met (none).

Study is resting-state functional connectivity, not a task-based emotion-regulation fMRI study. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (participants performing an emotion regulation task), I4 (reports task-related brain activation results). No exclusion criteria from E1/E2 are met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in humans where participants used imagery-focused emotion regulation during cues, and task-related BOLD responses (striatum) were modulated; meets inclusion criteria clearly.

Excluded because the study used MEG, not fMRI (I1 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (investigates automatic emotion regulation during a task), I3 (child participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met.

No task-based fMRI or task-related activation reported: the study examines structural integrity of the uncinate fasciculus (white-matter), likely using DTI, and links it to maltreatment and later symptoms. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in human participants examining emotion regulation (instructed reappraisal and uninstructed “respond naturally”) and reports task-related neural activation results (PFC, amygdala). Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation in human participants (depressed patients) and reports prefrontal activation predicting symptom trajectory over 6 months, satisfying I1-I4; no exclusion criteria are met.

Task-based fMRI in healthy human participants using attention-to-breath to regulate responses to aversive visual stimuli, with reported task-related brain activation (amygdala and prefrontal cortex) linked to regulation ability. Meets inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports a human study of cognitive reappraisal in younger and older adults (meets I2 and I3). Task-based fMRI with human younger and older adults employing cognitive reappraisal and selective attention to regulate emotional responses; reports neural connectivity during regulation. This satisfies inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, and I4 and no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract does not describe an emotion regulation task or instructed regulation — it assesses dispositional reappraisal during phobic stimulation (I2 not demonstrated). Inclusion met: I1, I3, I4. No exclusion criteria met.
EXCLUDED because inclusion criterion I1 (task-based fMRI) is not met: the study uses EEG rather than fMRI. Inclusion criteria met: I2, I3, I4. Exclusion criteria met: none (E1, E2 not applicable).

Task-based fMRI with 46 mothers viewing stressful vs. non-stressful child stimuli and reporting task-related brain activation; however the abstract does not state participants were instructed to regulate their emotions, so I2 is uncertain. No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human bereaved participants), I4 (task-related activation reported). Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation), reports task-related brain activation results, and involves human participants. Abstract reports a task-based pharmaco-fMRI study in humans using cognitive reappraisal of negative stimuli, with reported task-related activation and connectivity results; no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study with human participants viewing emotion-evoking visual stimuli and reports task-related brain activation differences between groups; meets inclusion criteria for task-based emotion regulation or viewing and reports activations. No exclusion criteria met.

Study reports task-based fMRI of human participants using a reappraisal (detachment-from-threat) emotion-regulation task and presents reappraisal-related brain activation results (shifts in lateral frontal cortex). Meets inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria apparent.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study in humans using a cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task, reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results, and includes healthy adult participants. All inclusion criteria are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract indicates a neuroimaging study of emotional cue processing but does not specify task-based fMRI, whether participants performed an emotion-regulation or passive viewing task, or report task-related activation results. Excluded: study used EEG (not task-based fMRI) so I1 not met, and did not involve an instructed emotion-regulation task (I2 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants) and I4 (reports task-related neural activation). No exclusion criteria were met (exclusion_criteria_applied=[]).

Abstract does not indicate participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (I2 not demonstrated). Study is task-based fMRI (I1), includes human participants (I3), and reports task-related activation (I4). No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study with human participants (45 women) who performed explicit reappraisal and an implicit placebo regulation while viewing disgusting visual stimuli; reports task-related brain activation and connectivity results. Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in human participants who decide whether to regulate emotional responses to visual (negative) images; it examines neural predictors and reports task-related brain activation results. This meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are evident.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants, young and older adults), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met. Excluded because the study used EEG/ERPs rather than task-based fMRI (I1 not met). The abstract does meet I2 (human emotion regulation task—positive reappraisal), I3 (human participants), and I4 (reports task-related neural activation results).

Abstract describes a task-based fMRI study using cognitive reappraisal of negative visual scenes that reduced negative affect and reports task-related brain activation (prefrontal cortex, amygdala). This satisfies inclusion criteria I1–I4; no exclusion criteria apply.

EXCLUDED because the study is not a task-based fMRI study (I1 not met). The abstract describes an EEG study of cognitive reappraisal (I2 met), with human participants (I3 met) and task-related brain activity reported (EEG; I4 met). No exclusion criteria met.

E2 met: task involved self-/other-referential processing (face-word relevance ratings) with no instruction to amplify or dampen emotion. Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in human participants examining cognitive reappraisal (instructed and spontaneous) and reports amygdala and prefrontal activation, so it meets inclusion criteria I1–I4. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study with human participants instructed to increase or decrease their affective responses to visual images. The abstract reports task-related brain activation results. All inclusion criteria (I1–I4) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract reports human participants with social anxiety and neural/behavioral responses but does not specify that tasks were fMRI-based or involved explicit emotion regulation (or pure viewing), nor does it state task-related brain activation results. Longitudinal task-based fMRI where adults performed effortful emotion regulation of negative stimuli; reports task-related activation (amygdala, ventrolateral/dorsolateral PFC). Meets I1-I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Study is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults reporting task-related activation (meets I1, I3, I4) but does not involve an emotion-regulation task with visual stimuli or instruction to regulate affect (does not meet I2). No exclusion criteria are triggered (none of E1–E2 apply).

Task-based fMRI study (N=26) of primiparous mothers using distraction to regulate emotions in response to infant crying; reports reduced amygdala activation with regulation. Satisfies I1,I2,I3,I4. No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI reported in Study 2), I3 (human participants), I4 (task-related brain activation results reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I2 (no emotion regulation task—participants were not instructed to regulate; study measured passive/individual differences in responses to fear-eliciting stimuli). Therefore excluded because I2 is not satisfied.

Abstract provides insufficient information to confirm task-based fMRI, specific emotion regulation task, visual stimuli, or reported brain activation. Include for full-text review to determine if inclusion criteria I1–I4 are met.

No evidence in abstract of a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm. No emotion-regulation task of visual stimuli was used: the study used an arithmetic task with auditory feedback measuring distress tolerance, not instructed cognitive reappraisal or similar. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (healthy human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). Inclusion IDs not met: I2 (no emotion-regulation task as defined).

Task-based fMRI with human adults using instructed emotion regulation (increase/decrease negative responses) during a task; reports ACC activation and connectivity related to errors (task-related brain activation). Fits inclusion criteria I1-I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports task-based fMRI in human adolescents during an emotion regulation task (including passive viewing of negative vs neutral visual stimuli) and reports task-related vmPFC–amygdala functional connectivity linked to psychopathology, matching the review objective and inclusion criteria.

Study uses implicit emotional processing (gender judgment) without instructions to regulate emotion. Exclusion IDs met: []. Study is a task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive reappraisal in human participants (69 female adults), reporting task-related brain activation correlated with real-life affect. It meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are apparent from the abstract.

Excluded (E2): study examines empathy for others' pain without instructions to amplify or dampen participants' emotional responses. Task-based real-time fMRI neurofeedback study in human adolescents (7–16) teaching up-/down-regulation of an emotion-regulation region (insula); reports task-related activation and connectivity. E1: This is a review/non-empirical paper (‘We review the research...’) and does not report original task-based fMRI data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Study reports a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy human (female) participants performing voluntary emotion regulation of emotional pictures and reports task-related brain activation results; matches I1, I2, I3, and I4. No exclusion criteria met.

E1 met: this paper is a systematic review summarizing imaging studies and does not present original human task-based fMRI data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Abstract reports a film-based emotion reactivity and regulation task performed in an MRI scanner, with age-related changes in emotional reactivity and reported brain activation (middle frontal gyrus). Fits task-based fMRI emotion regulation studies; no exclusion criteria met.

This is explicitly a review article examining models and prior fMRI findings, not an empirical study with original human data (meets exclusion E1). Excluded because the study uses resting-state fMRI pre/post an emotion provocation, not task-based fMRI or an explicit emotion-regulation instruction. Task-based fMRI in 40 healthy human participants viewing emotion-eliciting images while applying emotion regulation strategies (goal vs. implementation intentions). No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (task-based fMRI), I3 (human participants), I4 (reports task-related brain activation). No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (clinical human participants implied). Not an emotion-regulation task: abstract describes reading narratives with associated brain activation but no instruction to regulate emotion (I2 not met). No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: none. Task-based fMRI emotional face-processing study reporting task-related amygdala activation/habituation in human adolescents. Excluded (E1): This is a theoretical/review article without original human data. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not a task-based fMRI study), I2 (no emotion-regulation task reported), I4 (no task-related brain activation results); I3 not addressed.

Excluded because the study investigates reward-persistence and valuation, not emotion regulation of visual stimuli. Exclusion IDs met: []. Task-based fMRI in adolescents/young adults reporting rVLPFC activation to negative emotional words and links to emotion reappraisal and alcohol use. Task-based fMRI study examining anger provocation and regulation/distraction in human violent offenders and controls; reports task-related brain activation differences (prefrontal and limbic regions) specific to anger. No task-based fMRI or emotion-regulation task: study uses resting-state fMRI. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants with patient and control groups). Task-based fMRI using an emotion-word Stroop with emotional distractors; examines cognitive control of emotion in presence of affective stimuli and reports task-related brain activation in human adults. No task-based fMRI or task-related activation reported; study is structural (gray matter volume) correlational work in healthy humans. Inclusion met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion not met/demonstrated: I1, I2, I4. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract describes a task-based rt-fMRI study in healthy human participants who performed an emotion regulation task (down-regulation) while viewing aversive visual stimuli; it reports ROI and whole-brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review.

This is a theoretical/model paper (GANE extension) without original human data, so E1 applies. Task-based event-related fMRI study examining cognitive distraction as an anticipatory emotion regulation strategy; reports task-related brain activation (mPFC, amygdala) in human participants. Meets I1-I4; no exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study examining neural responses to threat cues during partner/stranger/no-handholding and reports threat-related brain activity, but it is unclear whether participants were instructed to perform an emotion regulation task (social support may be implicit). Include for full-text review to confirm I2.

Task-based fMRI with an intentional empathy (perspective-taking) task, healthy human subjects, and task-related hemodynamic activation reported. Abstract reports a task-based fMRI study in humans (older adults) who performed an emotion-regulation task (increase/decrease responses to negative pictures, i.e., reappraisal/ regulation), and presents task-related brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are met in the abstract.

Task-based fMRI study of an emotional Stroop (implicit emotion regulation/adaptation) in healthy adolescent girls reporting task-related brain activation linked to model-based regulatory states. No exclusion criteria met.

This is a narrative review without original human data (E1). It does not report a task-based fMRI emotion-regulation experiment or task-related activation results. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1, I2, I3, I4.

Abstract describes an empirical task-based rtfMRI neurofeedback study in healthy human participants targeting hippocampal activation to enhance emotion regulation. Exclusion criteria are not met. Full-text review needed to confirm relevance to the meta-analysis objective.

Human task-based rtfMRI study reporting task-related activation and voluntary modulation of emotional states via neurofeedback. No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (human participants measured). Study reports resting-state functional connectivity related to emotion recognition in adults born very preterm, not a task-based emotion regulation fMRI. Exclusion IDs met: none. Study uses diffusion tensor (DTI) structural MRI and reports white-matter integrity differences in dispositional emotion approach; it is not a task-based fMRI study and does not report task-related activation. Task-based fMRI in human adolescent participants reporting task-related brain activation. Abstract reports task-related neural activation (LPFC) during a frustration-inducing task in human children and examines emotion regulation-related facial expressions, but it does not specify fMRI or that participants performed an instructed emotion-regulation task. Abstract reports human participants using cognitive strategies to regulate reward expectation and reports neural correlates (striatum) and physiological measures, meeting criteria for emotion regulation task and task-related brain activation; fMRI modality not explicitly stated in abstract, so include for full-text review to confirm I1.

No task-based emotion regulation paradigm reported: this is a resting-state fMRI study. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (human participants). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (task-based fMRI), I2 (emotion regulation task), I4 (task-related brain activation results).

fulltext_screening_results.reason: Excluded because the study does not present or regulate emotional VISUAL stimuli (I7 not met). The fMRI task instructed emotion-introspection (a mindfulness/awareness strategy) and reports within-task contrasts (feel>think, feel>neutral) and whole-brain group analyses, but these contrasts reflect self-focused regulation from baseline without emotionally-valenced visual stimuli; only neutral pictures were used as distractors. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion-regulation-like strategy: emotion-introspection), I8 (clinical sample qualifies), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses), I11 (results described in text/supplement). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (emotional stimuli are VISUAL — not satisfied). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed explicit emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal: downregulate negative, upregulate positive) using visual stimuli (emotional pictures). It reports within-task contrasts (negative-downregulate > attend, positive-upregulate > attend, attend > baseline) and performs voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (FSL Randomise permutation tests) in standard (MNI) space, with results described as clusters/regions and figures/tables. A healthy control group is reported alongside the clinical rrMDD group. Full article text (methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs cognitive reappraisal during an emotion-regulation task (regulate > experience; I6). Emotional stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). The sample includes gambling disorder patients and healthy controls with group-level results reported separately (I8). The report includes within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g. ‘regulate’ > ‘experience’) and behavioural emotion-reduction scores (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates in MNI space and cluster-thresholding details (e.g. peak MNI x=-60,y=20,Z=32; thresholding and cluster sizes described), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria apply: this is empirical fMRI activation (not review), reports whole-brain activations (not ROI-only), includes within-group task effects (not only between-group), and is not an empathy/perspective-taking study without regulation. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (distancing, a form of cognitive reappraisal) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The sample includes a clinical group (PMDD) and healthy controls with results reported for groups separately. Analyses include within-task regulation contrasts (negative, far > negative, close) and unregulated contrasts (negative > neutral). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise group analyses with peak coordinates (MNI) and cluster-corrected results. The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

The study is excluded because the emotional stimuli that participants regulated were non-visual (auditory vignettes and spoken negative self-belief statements presented while participants had eyes closed). This fails inclusion criterion I7 (stimuli must be VISUAL). Relevant inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: reappraisal and acceptance), I8 (sample acceptable; patient and control groups reported), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported, e.g., reappraise > react, accept > react), I10 (whole-brain group-level analyses with corrected statistical maps), and I11 (results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that clearly meets all inclusion criteria: it uses an instructed cognitive emotion regulation paradigm (increase/decrease vs view) during fMRI (I6), with visual stimuli (static face photographs; I7), includes patient and matched control groups reported separately (I8), and reports within-task regulation contrasts ([increase+decrease] > view) behaviorally and neurally (I9). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported with cluster-corrected results and tables/coordinates (I10,I11). Methods, results, and discussion are fully present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. The study is therefore eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of instructed visual emotion regulation fMRI studies.

Full text reports an event-related task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation using cognitive reappraisal (decrease cue) with visual stimuli (IAPS images). It includes within-task contrasts relevant to the review (decrease > look negative; look negative > look neutral), reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-corrected results and peak coordinates described, and includes both clinical (SI) and control groups with separate comparisons. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because its emotional stimuli are words (visual word stimuli), which the review's criteria explicitly exclude (I7 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (eligible sample: non-clinical groups reported separately), I9 (reports within-task contrast: unpleasant > neutral), I10 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates), and I11 (results described in text/tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal/acceptance; participants were instructed to respond to ink color and ignore word meaning rather than to regulate emotion) and I7 (stimuli are words/sentences, which are excluded by the meta-analysis). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) applicable. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal: ‘regulate’ vs ‘attend’), using visual stimuli (neutral, fear, and OCD-related pictures). It reports within-task regulation contrasts (fear_regulate > attend; OCD_regulate > attend) and unregulated viewing contrasts (fear > neutral; OCD > neutral). The sample includes patients, unaffected siblings, and healthy controls with control-group results reported separately. Although ROI analyses are emphasized, the manuscript references supplemental whole-brain results and reports voxelwise SPM analyses (group-level contrasts), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, peak-coordinate results in standard space (supplementary materials). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs a cognitive emotion regulation strategy ('reality check' reappraisal) with visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures; transfer video clips). The authors report within-task contrasts related to regulation (regulate > view; regulate > baseline; view > baseline) and conduct group-level whole-brain analyses (voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not non-empirical, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group task effects, and is not an empathy/perspective-taking-only study).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to engage in a self-referential emotion regulation strategy (imagining/engaging oneself in positive-social scenes), using visual stimuli (IAPS/NAPS/GAPED images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (regulation > viewing; positive > neutral; interaction), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and FWE correction, and full methods/results/discussion. All inclusion criteria relevant to the review are met and none of the exclusion criteria apply (the study is not non-empirical, does not report only ROI or connectivity-only results, and includes within-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete. Therefore I include this study for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal during presentation of visual IAPS images and compares reappraise versus view conditions. The sample includes PTSD patients and healthy controls with group-level results reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise>view), and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (voxel-wise p<.001, cluster-wise pFWE<.05) with reported activation peaks. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The full text reports an original, task-based fMRI study in SAD patients using an instructed cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task (Reappraise vs Look Negative) with visual stimuli (IAPS images). The analysis includes within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraise > Look Negative) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates and corrected cluster thresholds. The methods, results, and discussion are present and sufficient. All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-visual stimuli, or non-empirical article). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). It reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > attend negative; suppress > attend negative), conducts group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (with FWE cluster correction) and provides peak coordinates; both patient and control groups are included and within-group task effects are reported. All required inclusion criteria are therefore met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This article is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (self-focused reappraisal to increase and decrease negative emotion) during presentation of visual stimuli (angry and neutral faces). It reports within-task contrasts (view-angry > view-neutral; increase > view-angry; decrease > view-angry; within- and between-group contrasts) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (cluster-thresholded maps and tables of activations). The sample includes a clinical group (MDD) and healthy controls with results reported separately. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied.

This is a task-based fMRI study in adolescents that instructed an emotion-regulation strategy (recall of positive autobiographical memories; “try to feel what you felt then”) paired to visual stimuli (happy self-face images), satisfying an instructed regulation manipulation. The stimuli are visual (static face images). The sample includes clinical (depressed) and healthy adolescents. The paper reports within-task contrasts (feedback+self-face > count-backwards+other-face) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses using standard thresholds and reports peak coordinates (e.g., hippocampus [34 −34 −10]; [−36 −26 −14]), fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. The study does not meet exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, not an empathy/perspective-taking-only task). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative affect while viewing visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise Negative > Attend Negative; Attend Negative > Attend Neutral) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. Sample details and task methods are fully described. Although resting-state connectivity analyses are also reported, task activation maps meeting inclusion criteria are clearly provided. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This full-text describes a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed participants to downregulate emotion via distancing (a reappraisal strategy) while viewing visual pictures (negative, positive, neutral). The sample includes acute anorexia nervosa patients and matched healthy controls with separate group analyses. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to the review (negative watch > neutral; negative watch > negative distance; negative watch < negative distance) and provides voxelwise results with peak coordinates in standard space (MNI), including mention of whole-brain/exploratory results (Fig. S1) and reported cluster peaks. Analyses are not limited to ROI/SVC-only results. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion-regulation task (affect labeling vs gender labeling), with visual stimuli (photographs of faces). Sample includes clinical (SAD) and healthy control groups. The paper reports within-task contrasts (affect label > gender label) and pre/post treatment paired analyses, and conducts whole-brain, voxelwise psychophysiological interaction (PPI) analyses with whole-brain correction and reported clusters/coordinates. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; not only connectivity without task activation maps; within-group effects are reported; not an empathy-only task). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria: participants were exposed to auditory script-driven imagery (not VISUAL stimuli), and they were instructed to imagine scenes to provoke emotion but were not instructed to use any emotion-regulation strategy. Specifically, inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports within-task contrasts such as anger>baseline and aggression>baseline), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates), and I11 (results reported in text/tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy), I7 (regulated stimuli are not visual). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive reappraisal using visual stimuli in OCD patients and healthy controls, and it reports within-task contrasts (regulate > maintain) at the ICA component/network level. However, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps for the regulation contrasts with peak coordinates in a standard stereotactic space (the main statistical tests for the key task contrasts are performed on ICA component time-course beta-weights using SPSS rather than voxelwise SPM second-level contrasts with reported coordinates). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I10 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map with peak coordinates). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion E4 met: the study reports only ROI-based analyses (average activations from 70 anatomical ROIs used in random forest models) and does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map with peak coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation — cognitive reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli — IAPS images), I8 (sample includes clinical participants; eligible), I9 (within-task conditions/contrasts: maintain and reappraise). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level map reported). The full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Because the review requires a whole-brain task activation map (I10) and this paper provides only ROI-based results, it must be excluded under E4.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed cognitive reappraisal (an emotion regulation strategy) while participants viewed visual negative and neutral images (IAPS). The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > Look-Negative and Look-Negative > Look-Neutral) and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and FWE-corrected results. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text (not truncated). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I9, I10 and I11. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is empirical (not E3), includes whole-brain activation maps (not only ROI, so not E4), reports activation contrasts (not only connectivity, so not E5), includes within-task effects (not only between-group contrasts, so not E6), and it is not an empathy/perspective-taking study lacking regulation instructions (not E7). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in which participants performed an instructed reappraisal task (Reappraise/Decrease vs Look) using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures) and additional face-viewing tasks. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise Negative vs Look Negative) and unregulated viewing (Look Negative vs Neutral). Voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses were conducted and reported (clusters/coordinates referenced in supplemental tables), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Sample (clinical PTSD) is acceptable. Although some ROI analyses are described, whole-brain voxelwise results are also presented. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise-negative) using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The analysis includes within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraise > attend-negative; attend-negative > attend-neutral) and whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses (3dMVM; cluster-thresholding with Monte Carlo correction), with results reported in the text and supplementary materials. The sample includes both clinical (BD, SZ) and healthy control groups with separate group-level reporting. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and supplementary tables/figures are referenced for coordinates/details. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This is a task-based fMRI study of fear conditioning/extinction using visual CS (rooms/colored lamps) in ADHD vs controls. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task contrasts, e.g., CS+ vs CS-; extinction contrasts), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis with MNI coordinates), I11 (coordinates and results clearly reported). However the study does NOT instruct an emotion regulation strategy (no cognitive reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other instructed regulation); it examines conditioned fear/extinction without regulation instructions, so I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded because it fails to satisfy I6 (instructed emotion regulation).

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed cognitive reappraisal using visual video stimuli with SAD and HC groups (meets I5, I6, I7, I8). However, the paper reports ROI-based connectivity (DEPNA) analyses and behavioral ratings rather than any group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps or peak coordinates. It does not present within-task whole-brain contrasts (e.g., reappraise > watch) or voxelwise tables/figures, so inclusion criteria I9 and I10 are not satisfied. Therefore the study falls under exclusions for reporting only ROI/connectivity analyses without accompanying whole‑brain task activation results (E4, E5). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (and reports the reappraise > attend-negative contrast), uses visual stimuli (IAPS images), includes patient and healthy control groups with separate reporting, and presents within-task contrasts and group-level whole-brain analyses with reported peak coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing complete assessment against the inclusion/exclusion criteria.

Excluded because the study does not meet inclusion criterion I7: emotional stimuli are not visual. The neurofeedback task required participants to recall positive autobiographical memories (an internal/imagery-based emotional induction), not to view or regulate responses to external visual emotional stimuli. Met inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy was used), I9 (within-task contrasts/condition beta for the ‘happy’ neurofeedback blocks were reported and used in analysis), I10 (whole-brain, voxelwise group-level mapping with reported peak coordinates), and I11 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Because the meta-analysis specifically targets studies regulating or viewing visual emotional stimuli, this study is not eligible despite meeting several other criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study (n-back) that manipulated emotional state via olfactory stimuli (negative vs neutral) and reports whole-brain group-level activation coordinates. However, the study does not meet key criteria for the review: (1) the emotional stimuli are olfactory (non-visual), not visual images or videos, so I7 is not met; (2) there was no instructed emotion-regulation task (no reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or similar instructions), so I6 is not met. The study does meet I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample criteria: includes clinical and control groups reported), I9 (reports within-task emotional contrast negative vs neutral), I10 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps with coordinates), and I11 (results reported as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore EXCLUDED because it fails required inclusion criteria I6 and I7.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional face stimuli with patients and controls and reports emotional vs neutral contrasts, but it does not meet the review's requirements for inclusion. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample includes patient and control groups), I9 (reports an unregulated viewing contrast: emotional > neutral). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; task required ignoring emotional expressions rather than instructing reappraisal or other regulation), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-activation peak coordinates are reported in standard space for univariate activation contrasts; the reported peak coordinates pertain to PPI connectivity results). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (the paper reports primarily seed-based/task-dependent connectivity [PPI] results without accompanying whole-brain task activation maps/coordinates). Because E5 is met, the study must be excluded.

Full text meets all inclusion criteria: (I5) task-based fMRI; (I6) instructed emotion regulation using cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise condition); (I7) visual stimuli (IAPS pictures, neutral images); (I8) sample includes clinical (GAD) and healthy control groups reported separately; (I9) reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > Look-Neutral; Look-Negative > Look-Neutral); (I10) whole-brain voxel-wise analyses with cluster correction and peak MNI coordinates; (I11) results reported in text/figures. No exclusion criteria are met. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation (accept, worry, suppress) in a clinical GAD sample and reports within-task contrasts and group-level maps. However, the emotional stimuli were personally relevant worry statements presented as text (word/sentence stimuli: “What if…?”), not visual images, videos, or film clips. Inclusion criterion I7 requires regulated stimuli to be VISUAL (e.g., IAPS images, photographs, faces, scenes, or video clips); studies using only word/sentence stimuli are excluded. Therefore the study fails I7 and must be excluded. Other inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation including acceptance), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (within-task contrasts reported), and I10/I11 (group-level whole-brain results/maps are reported/illustrated). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) appear to apply. Full text appears complete.

This full-text reports an event-related, task-based fMRI experiment using an instructed cognitive reappraisal strategy (distancing) with visual IAPS images; includes behavioral and neural within-task contrasts (e.g., distance>baseline, spontaneous_negative>baseline); presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE inference; and reports connectivity and ROI analyses alongside whole-brain maps. The article contains full introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. These elements satisfy all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed an emotion-regulation strategy (distraction via a MEMORIZE vs VIEW paradigm) while presenting visual emotional stimuli (negative and neutral pictures from IAPS/EmoPics). The sample includes a clinical group (BPD patients) and control groups. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., MEMORIZE>VIEW, NEGATIVE>NEUTRAL), performs group- and time-level whole-brain voxelwise second-level analyses, and provides peak coordinates and cluster results. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion, limitations, refs) is present. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. The full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (face-matching) with a within-task contrast (face-matching > shape-matching) isolating emotional processing.
