Sample comprises healthy adult community volunteers. All inclusion criteria for the review are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Full text is a complete empirical task-based fMRI study with whole-brain group analyses (coordinates reported). However, it does NOT meet key inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis: (1) the task does not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy such as cognitive reappraisal (I6 not met) — participants control/stop nociceptive stimulation rather than being instructed to reappraise visual stimuli; (2) the regulated stimuli are not visual (I7 not met) — stimuli are noxious electrical (somatosensory), not images or video; (3) the within-task contrasts concern perceived control over pain rather than instructed emotion regulation of visual stimuli (I9 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of visual emotional stimuli (facial emotion matching) with whole-brain group analyses and within-task contrasts (face > shape). However, the task does not include any instructed emotion regulation (e.g., reappraisal, distancing) — participants simply matched emotional faces vs shapes rather than being told to up- or down-regulate their emotional responses. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (instruction of an emotion regulation strategy). All other applicable inclusion criteria are met (see inclusion_criteria_applied). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of visual emotional stimuli (faces) with whole-brain task-evoked analyses and unregulated viewing contrasts; however the in-scanner paradigm was passive face viewing with a simple button press and did not instruct participants to use any emotion regulation strategy. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation task). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (whole-brain group-level analyses), I11 (results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because I6 is not satisfied.

Study 2 is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation that instructs cognitive reappraisal (CHANGE) while participants view visual negative images (IAPS) and neutral images. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (decrease negative > look negative) and unregulated viewing contrasts (look negative > look neutral), includes bilateral amygdala ROI analyses and whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses (reported with voxelwise threshold and table of coordinates), and provides sufficient methodological detail and results (behavioral ratings, ROI betas, whole-brain clusters). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, non-empirical article, empathy-only tasks) are met. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and should be included in the meta-analysis.

Exclusion reason: E4 (reports only ROI / small-volume-corrected results with no accompanying whole-brain voxelwise task activation map) applies. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: facial photographs), I8 (sample includes patients and controls), I9 (reports within-task contrasts related to regulation/adaptation). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (an emotion regulation strategy was not instructed — the study examines implicit, non-instructed regulation), I10 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation map reported; results are restricted to ROI/SVC analyses). Because the meta-analysis requires instructed emotion regulation (I6) and whole-brain task activation reporting (I10), the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of visual emotional stimuli in older adults that reports within-task contrasts (iI vs cI) and whole-brain results and coordinates; however, the key exclusion is that emotion regulation was not instructed. The task measures implicit emotion conflict adaptation rather than an instructed regulation strategy (e.g., cognitive reappraisal, acceptance, distancing). Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (fMRI task with an instructed emotion regulation strategy) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: faces), I8 (sample: older adults), I9 (reports within-task contrast related to emotion regulation: iI vs cI), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates), I11 (results reported clearly in text/tables). Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) . Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (“reality checking” cognitive reappraisal) during anticipation and perception of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (exp negative > exp neutral; perc negative > perc neutral) for the groups and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLM analyses with cluster-correction; results and supplementary materials are described. The sample (patients with SAD) is an eligible participant group for the review. Thus the study meets the meta-analysis objective of fMRI studies comparing regulation vs unregulated viewing of visual emotional stimuli and provides whole-brain activation evidence suitable for coordinate-based synthesis. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, within-group effects reported, not an empathy/perspective-taking-only task).

This study should be excluded because it reports only task-dependent seed-based connectivity (PPI) analyses without reporting a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map/coordinates for the main task contrasts in this paper (Exclusion E5). Although the work uses a task-based fMRI design with visual IAPS stimuli and reports within-task contrasts used in PPI (I5, I7, I9) and includes an appropriate sample (I8), it does not instruct an explicit emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met) and it does not provide whole-brain task activation results in this manuscript (I10 not met). Full text appears complete. Therefore it fails exclusion criterion E5 and does not meet all required inclusion criteria (notably I6 and I10), so it must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed cognitive reappraisal (reduce vs. maintain) while participants viewed visual stimuli (CAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (reduce vs. maintain), and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates (FDR-corrected maps and reported x,y,z). Sample is healthy adults and all relevant inclusion criteria for emotion regulation fMRI studies are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-groups-only, or non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study does not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses (inclusion criterion I6 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli - IAPS images), I8 (clinical and control samples reported separately), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts, e.g., negative > neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported), I11 (whole-brain results clearly described). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the paper is ineligible for a meta-analysis that requires an instructed emotion-regulation task.

This is a study-design/protocol RCT describing task-based fMRI with visual stimuli and planned within-task contrasts, but it does not report group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical results. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies: children/adolescents), I9 (reports/plans within-task contrasts such as neutral vs fearful faces and winning vs frustration). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal is given; tasks measure spontaneous regulation/recovery but do not instruct regulation), I10 (no group-level whole-brain statistical maps or peak coordinates reported), I11 (no whole-brain results presented in text/tables/figures). Exclusion criterion applicable: E3 (methods/design paper without original whole-brain fMRI data). Full text appears complete (protocol/methods present), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs participants to upregulate positive emotions via autobiographical memory recall with real-time neurofeedback (meets I6). The sample is acceptable (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g. train > rest; happy > rest) and training-run comparisons (I9), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates (I10, I11). However, the emotional elicitation and regulation in this study are driven by internally-generated autobiographical memory recall rather than externally-presented visual emotional stimuli. The review’s eligibility requires that regulated stimuli be VISUAL (I7). Because the regulated stimuli here are non-visual (scripted/imagery-based autobiographical recall), the study does not meet I7 and therefore is ineligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to downregulate emotion using cognitive reappraisal while viewing visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts (decrease vs. observe; observe negative vs. neutral), conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster threshold Z>2.0, p=.05 corrected) with reported regional activation and PPI connectivity results, and provides ROI analyses. The sample includes euthymic bipolar I subjects and a healthy control group with results reported separately. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met: the paper is empirical, includes whole-brain task activation maps (not ROI-only), and reports within-group task effects (not only between-group contrasts) while also including connectivity as additional analyses. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual emotional stimuli (faces) with whole-brain group-level analyses and reports unregulated viewing contrasts (fear > neutral). However, participants were not instructed to use an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal, distancing, or similar instructions), so inclusion criterion I6 (regulation instructed) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample eligibility), I9 (reports within-task contrasts/un-modulated event contrasts), I10 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with coordinates), I11 (results reported in text/tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy—task asked subjects to rate likelihoods, not to up-/down-regulate emotion), I7 (stimuli comprised written event descriptions/words, i.e. sentence stimuli, which are excluded by I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) directly apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore EXCLUDED on the basis of failing I6 and I7.

The full text is a complete empirical task-based fMRI study that meets all inclusion criteria: it instructs emotion regulation (Decrease/Increase reappraisal), uses visual stimuli (IAPS negative and neutral images), includes a clinical MDD group with healthy controls reported separately, reports within-task contrasts of interest (Decrease Negative > Look Negative; Increase Negative > Look Neutral), and provides whole-brain voxelwise group-level results with peak coordinates and corrected thresholds. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not a review, does not report only ROI/partial-coverage results (it includes whole-brain FLAME analyses), is not exclusively connectivity/resting-state, and is not an empathy/perspective-taking task without regulation instructions. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (static facial expressions) with a mood induction paradigm (happiness and sadness). The authors created subject-level contrasts for each emotional condition (sadness vs baseline; happiness vs baseline) and performed whole-brain, group-level random-effects SPM analyses reporting cluster-level results across the whole brain. The sample includes both first-episode schizophrenia patients and matched healthy controls with results reported separately and compared. Although the task instructs participants to 'become as happy/sad as possible' (an emotion induction rather than an explicit cognitive reappraisal/regulation instruction), the paper reports unregulated viewing/emotion>baseline contrasts which satisfy inclusion criterion I9. The study therefore meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample), I9 (within-task unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis), and I11 (reporting whole-brain results). I6 (explicit instructed regulation strategy such as reappraisal) is not met, but is not required because unregulated viewing contrasts are present. Minor ambiguity: the excerpt does not display coordinate tables in the provided text, but whole-brain cluster results and methods indicate voxelwise analyses were performed. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses (no reappraisal/distancing/acceptance instruction). Exclusion criterion met: E7 (empathy/perspective-taking tasks without instruction to amplify/dampen own emotion). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli used for ER and EPT tasks: face photographs and scenes), I8 (sample qualifies; clinical group reported separately), I9 (reports within-task/unregulated viewing task activation), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinates/cluster results), I11 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy; tasks assess empathy/perspective-taking/affective responsiveness without regulation instructions). Because I6 is required and E7 is directly applicable, the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (Hariri face-matching task) and reports within-task contrasts of unregulated viewing (negative > neutral and happy > neutral). The sample (n=88, ages 21–85) is appropriate. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates and cluster-level inference (voxel p<0.001, cluster p<0.05 FWE), and results (coordinates, clusters) are described in the text and tables. Although participants were not instructed to regulate emotion (no instructed reappraisal), the meta-analysis objective includes studies that view stimuli without regulating; the study therefore satisfies the unregulated-viewing pathway (I9). All other applicable inclusion criteria (I5, I7, I8, I10, I11) are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (acupoint tapping) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (phobia-related and fear-inducing pictures). It reports within-task contrasts comparing regulation (tapping) versus viewing, and presents group-level whole-brain analyses (FWE-corrected) with coordinates/tables. The sample (participants with fear of flying) is an eligible clinical group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the manuscript appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive emotion regulation (reappraisal/distancing: Decrease vs Look), using visual IAPS images as stimuli, with both behavioral and fMRI analyses. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Decrease > Look-Negative, Decrease > Look-Neutral) and decision-related contrasts, and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results thresholded at p<0.05 FWE with MNI coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (distancing, an instance of cognitive reappraisal; I6) while participants view visual stimuli (static pictures; I7). The sample includes a clinical group (weight-recovered AN) and matched healthy controls reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation and viewing (e.g., negative watch > neutral, positive watch > positive distance; I9). The authors state that secondary analyses included whole-brain analyses (with results and further details referenced in the supplementary material), satisfying the requirement for group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps/coordinates (I10) and acceptable reporting in supplementary materials (I11). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met.

This study is a resting-state, seed-based functional connectivity fMRI experiment probing effects of acute tryptophan depletion and MAOA genotype. It does not include any task-based emotion regulation paradigm or instructions to regulate emotional responses, nor does it present within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look) or unregulated viewing contrasts of visual emotional stimuli. Therefore it fails the core inclusion criteria requiring task-based emotion regulation and task-evoked contrasts. Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the study reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity analyses without a task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample: healthy adult males). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation), I7 (visual emotional stimuli/regulation of visual stimuli), I9 (within-task regulation/viewing contrasts), I10 (task-evoked whole-brain maps). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion (E4) applies: the fMRI results are reported using region-of-interest analyses (selected ROIs and partial-least-squares on those ROIs) with no accompanying whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps provided. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI subset reported), I8 (sample qualifies), and I9 (reports BOLD response to negative words — an unregulated viewing-type contrast). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (the fMRI task did NOT instruct an emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal; it required emotion identification and digit-sorting, not instructed regulation), I7 (emotional stimuli were words/sentences rather than the visual images/films required by the review), and I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise maps reported). Because E4 is met and key inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I10) are not satisfied, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

The article reports a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that includes an instructed emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) using visual stimuli (IAPS images) and faces. It reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraise > Look-Negative) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (FWE-corrected clusters). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text contains methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that used visual stimuli (proposer faces and offer displays) during the ultimatum game (I7). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing unfair vs. fair offers (unregulated viewing of negatively valenced vs. neutral/positive social stimuli), which satisfies the requirement for an unregulated viewing contrast (I9). The study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected clusters and tabulated results (whole-brain maps/peaks referenced in Table 2), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement (I10) and acceptable reporting formats (I11). The sample includes AUD and healthy control groups with separate reporting (I8). Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction was given (I6 not met), the protocol and contrasts align with the review scope allowing unregulated viewing contrasts. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of instructed cognitive reappraisal using visual IAPS images in adolescent participants; it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation — reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), and I9 (within-task regulation contrasts: Decrease>Look and Increase>Look). However, the paper reports hypothesis-driven ROI/parcel analyses focused on DLPFC and does not provide a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain activation map with peak coordinates in standard space (inclusion I10 NOT met). Because the study reports only ROI/parcel-focused results without a qualifying whole-brain voxelwise coordinate map, it falls under exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI/SMC results or no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis that requires whole-brain coordinate data.

Full text complete. Excluded because the fMRI task does not meet the review's required task or stimulus modality. Specifically: (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample acceptable: AUD patients and matched controls), I9 (reports within-task unregulated contrasts such as stress > neutral), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates), I11 (results clearly described). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy — participants underwent guided imagery; no reappraisal/distancing/other regulation instruction), I7 (stimuli are script-driven auditory imagery, not visual stimuli). Because both I6 and I7 are required, the study is ineligible for inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli in children and adults and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain analyses in the text; however it does NOT meet the review’s required criterion that an emotion regulation strategy be explicitly instructed (I6). Participants experienced induced mood via winning/losing points but were not instructed to use a regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, suppression, distancing). Additionally, the provided full text does not present peak coordinates for group-level whole-brain statistical maps in standard space (Talairach/MNI) in the excerpt, raising uncertainty about satisfying I10. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (within-task contrasts/unregulated viewing contrasts), I11 (whole-brain results described in text). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed regulation), I10 (peak coordinates not provided in the available full text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) were triggered based on the provided full text. Full text appears complete: fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study is a combined 1H/31P MR spectroscopy investigation, not a task-based fMRI experiment. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I8 (sample: includes participant groups and controls). Inclusion IDs NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation task/cognitive reappraisal), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli presented during an fMRI task), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or viewing contrasts reported), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked fMRI maps with peak coordinates), I11 (no reporting of whole-brain fMRI results). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper does not meet the required fMRI/task-based inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (faces) with whole-brain analyses and appropriate task contrasts; however the task manipulates emotion labeling (an incidental/implicit form of emotion regulation) rather than instructing participants to employ an explicit emotion regulation strategy (e.g., cognitive reappraisal, acceptance, instructed control). Inclusion criterion I6 requires an instructed emotion regulation strategy. Although the study provides relevant contrasts (emotion labeling vs. emotion matching/gender labeling) and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain group analyses, it does not meet the explicit requirement that regulation is instructed. Therefore it must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation (positive suppress vs maintain), using visual stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (positive suppress > positive maintain) and whole-brain voxelwise group analyses with peak coordinates and cluster correction. Both patient (MDD) and healthy control groups are included and reported separately. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, stimuli, task, image acquisition/analysis), Results (coordinates, statistics), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete for screening. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text describes an empirical, task-based fMRI study in which participants were explicitly instructed to use emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (15-sec disgust-eliciting film clips). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (e.g., reappraise > watch-negative, suppress > watch-negative) and unregulated viewing contrasts (watch-negative > watch-neutral). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported with Talairach coordinates and tables, and sample characteristics (healthy adult females) are provided. The manuscript includes complete Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; within-task contrasts are reported; not an empathy/perspective-taking-only design). Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and should be INCLUDED.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I5) task-based fMRI with BOLD acquisition; (I6) instructed emotion regulation (distancing/’far’ reappraisal); (I7) visual stimuli (IAPS and photographs); (I8) sample includes healthy adolescents and young adults (ages 10.5–22.9); (I9) reports within-task regulation contrasts (regulation/negative > reactivity/negative, reactivity/negative > reactivity/neutral); (I10) whole-brain group-level analyses reported (mixed-effects whole-brain models with coordinates and cluster thresholds); (I11) whole-brain results presented in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply: this is empirical original fMRI data, includes whole-brain analyses (not only ROI or connectivity), reports within-group task effects, and is a regulation (not mere perspective-taking) paradigm. Full text is complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

Full text incomplete: only title, authors, journal, and DOI metadata provided; core article content (methods, results, discussion) is not present. Cannot verify required inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I8 (sample reporting/group data), I9 (within-task emotion-regulation or viewing contrasts), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps with peak coordinates), I11 (reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria can be assessed from the available metadata (no E3–E7 met based on provided info). Because essential information to determine eligibility is missing, the study is excluded pending full-text availability.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (Increase/Decrease) while presenting visual IAPS pictures, with a healthy adult sample. The manuscript reports within-task contrasts (Increase > Look-Negative; Decrease > Look-Negative), performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses with reported activations/ROIs and coordinates, and includes univariate results in addition to PPI connectivity. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met (connectivity analyses are present but not the only reported analyses). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (Increase, Decrease, Look) using cognitive reappraisal (I6). Stimuli are visual (IAPS pictures and high-arousal film clips) meeting visual-stimulus inclusion (I7). The sample is healthy adults with reported group details (I8). Analyses report within-task contrasts (Increase>Look, Decrease>Look, Increase>Decrease) and MVPA decoding of regulation goals (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise univariate analyses with MNI coordinates and FWE correction are reported in tables (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and participants were instructed to modulate their own emotional responses). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal of visual (IAPS) images in healthy adults and reports within-task comparisons between negative, reappraisal, and neutral conditions. However, the paper does not present group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps or peak coordinates in standard space. Instead fMRI data are reduced to AAL ROI means and cluster-based masks, and results are reported as ROI/Z-score summaries. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise evidence (I10) and meets exclusion criterion E4 (only ROI/region-averaged results reported). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I10. Exclusion criteria met: E4. Full text appears complete. Given the lack of whole-brain voxelwise maps/coordinates, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The article reports a task-based fMRI cognitive reappraisal paradigm (Regulate vs Maintain; Maintain vs Observe) using visual picture stimuli, with adult clinical (obese) and healthy control groups reported separately. Within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation are presented. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described with peak coordinates in MNI space and cluster-corrected results. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. The full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study (N=21 healthy adults) that explicitly instructed cognitive reappraisal strategies (up- and down-regulation) during task performance. The regulated stimuli are visual: IAPS pictures used in training and photographs of proposers' faces presented during the Ultimatum Game; regulation was applied during stimulus/offer presentation. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Down > Look, Up > Look, and Down < Look < Up) and contrasts for regulated decisions, and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and tables (FWE-corrected clusters). The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and distraction) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS and matched images). The sample (18 healthy adult women) is appropriate, and the paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look negative; distract > look negative) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates, tables, and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual stimuli (faces and bodies) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (Bodies > Scrambled, Faces > Scrambled) with group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (MNI coordinates). However, the fMRI task did not instruct participants to use any emotion regulation strategy (e.g., cognitive reappraisal, distancing, acceptance); participants passively viewed images with occasional attractiveness ratings. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (instruction to regulate). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

The full text is complete. Exclusion decision because the fMRI task did NOT instruct an emotion regulation strategy (I6 not met): participants viewed partner/stranger facial expressions with no instructions to regulate (authors state there were no explicit instructions to regulate). The study does meet multiple other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—static face photographs), I8 (acceptable sample), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts such as partner negative > partner neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates), and I11 (results reported in text/tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria apply (none of E3–E7 are met). Therefore excluded for failing to satisfy all required inclusion criteria (specifically I6).

This paper reports a task-based fMRI experiment (Experiment 3) in which participants were instructed to cognitively up- and down-regulate emotional responses (reappraisal: Increase, Maintain, Decrease) to visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). It includes within-task contrasts (Increase vs Maintain, Decrease vs Maintain, conjunctions), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space and tables/figures (FWE-corrected results reported). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all meta-analysis inclusion requirements.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly instructs emotion regulation strategies (Detachment, Reinterpretation, Distraction, Expressive Suppression) using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., ‘Regulate Negative’ > ‘Permit Negative’, ‘Permit Negative’ > ‘Permit Neutral’) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and FWE-corrected results. The sample and methods meet the review’s participant and analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, within-task effects reported, and not an empathy/perspective-taking study without regulation instruction). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (ignore negative expression and rate attractiveness) using visual stimuli (photographs of faces). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing high-control (reappraise) > low-control conditions for emotion, and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates (Table 2, conjunction analyses). Sample (healthy young adults) is eligible. Full text includes introduction, methods, behavioral and imaging results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group task contrasts, not an empathy/perspective-taking only task). Therefore it meets I5–I11 and should be included for the meta-analysis of emotion regulation to visual stimuli.

Excluded because the regulated stimuli are personalized written statements (word/sentence stimuli displayed as text), not visual images or videos; this fails inclusion criterion I7 (visual stimuli). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation via cognitive reappraisal), I8 (sample acceptable across ages), I9 (reports within-task contrasts such as Reappraisal–Neutral and Worry–Neutral), and I10/I11 (whole-brain analyses/interaction cluster and whole-brain gPPI maps are reported/mentioned, with results in text/supplement). No exclusion criteria appear to be met (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate emotion elicited by visual stimuli (negative facial photographs). The sample is healthy adults, and the paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise-Neg vs Maintain-Neg; Maintain-Neg vs Look-Neut). Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates, cluster thresholds, and figures/tables. Full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal during viewing of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS photographs) in younger and older adults. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Reappraise > Experience and Experience > Reappraise), conducts whole-brain group-level analyses with voxelwise thresholds and reports peak coordinates/tables, and includes behavioral and neuroimaging methods, results and discussion. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (an emotion-regulation strategy) of visual social-affective images and also includes an unregulated viewing condition. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (reappraise > look-negative; look-negative > reappraise; look-negative > look-neutral) and uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates. The sample (adolescents and young adults) meets the eligible participant criteria. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal of visual (IAPS) images and reports the within-task contrast ReappNeg vs LookNeg, with healthy participants and appropriate methods; however, the full text reports analyses based on region-of-interest (AAL-derived ROI beta weights) and PCA/classification of ROI data and does not present a group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation map or peak coordinates in standard space. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I10 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map with peak coordinates). This triggers exclusion criterion E4 (reports ONLY ROI results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I10. Exclusion criterion applied: E4.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (reappraisal: upregulation, downregulation, permitting) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., upregulate > permit, downregulate > permit, upregulate > downregulate) and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with cluster results and MNI coordinates. The sample includes frontal lobe epilepsy patients and healthy controls with results reported for groups separately. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs emotion regulation via cognitive reappraisal (EER task: upregulate/downregulate), using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures) and an additional attentional control task with pictures. The sample includes clinical groups and healthy controls with group-level results reported separately. Within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Downregulate > View) are reported. Analyses are whole-brain, random-effects GLMs with reported peak coordinates and corrected thresholds. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-without-regulation) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and should be included in the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study does not meet several key inclusion criteria for this review. Inclusion met: I5 (task-based fMRI data were collected) and I8 (adult sample). Inclusion NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy—participants were asked to think about/how statements made them feel, not to reappraise or otherwise regulate), I7 (stimuli were sentences/words/self-referential statements, i.e., linguistic rather than visual images or film/video), I9 (the paper does not report any within-task regulation or viewing contrasts such as reappraise>look or emotion>baseline), and I10 (no whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation map reported for an emotion-regulation contrast). No exclusion criteria from E3–E7 are directly triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is not eligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because the emotional stimuli are words (rejection-themed words) presented as text. Inclusion criterion I7 explicitly excludes studies whose emotional stimuli are word or sentence stimuli. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample includes children), I9 (reports an unregulated viewing contrast: rejection > neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinates), and I11 (results reported in text/tables/supplement). It does not meet I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Only the article abstract and metadata are provided (fulltext_incomplete). The abstract indicates a task-based fMRI study addressing cognitive reappraisal, so I5 and I6 appear to be met. However the full text is missing key details needed to confirm other inclusion criteria: stimulus modality (visual) is not specified (I7 not verifiable), participant/sample details are not reported in the abstract (I8 not verifiable), no within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look) or explicit task-evoked statistical maps/peak coordinates are provided in the abstract (I9,I10,I11 not verifiable). The study focuses on functional connectivity methods, raising the possibility that whole-brain task activation maps may not be reported, but this cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone. Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot verify all required inclusion criteria, so the study is excluded from the review at this stage pending full text access.

This full text reports a task-based fMRI experiment in which participants were instructed to regulate emotion using cognitive reappraisal (increase, decrease, view) while viewing visual threat-related IAPS pictures. It includes subject/sample details (24 healthy females), experimental methods, within-task contrasts (increase > view, decrease > view, view > neutral), trial-by-trial and group-level random-effects fMRI analyses, and reports whole-brain results with peak coordinates (tables and figures). Peripheral physiological and self-report data are also reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes both unregulated viewing (observe only faces vs fixation) and an instructed affect-labeling task (emotion-label vs gender-label). Affect labeling is an instructed verbal strategy shown to modulate emotional responses and is treated here as an emotion-regulation instruction. Stimuli are visual (static face images). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (emotion label > gender label) and unregulated viewing contrasts (observe > fixation). Analyses include group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps with peak MNI coordinates and cluster thresholds. Sample is healthy adult participants. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; not only connectivity; reports within-task effects). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that meets all inclusion criteria: it implements an instructed emotion regulation paradigm using cognitive reappraisal (I6) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures; I7), acquires task-based fMRI data (I5), and reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g. Reappraise > Attend, Attend > Reappraise) (I9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates in MNI space and FWE-corrected results (I10,I11). The sample is healthy adult participants and therefore qualifies (I8). The full paper contains introduction, methods, results and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical (not a review), includes whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only), reports task activations (not only connectivity or between-group-only contrasts), and is not an empathy/perspective-taking task without regulation instructions. Hence the study should be INCLUDED in the review.

This full-text reports an event-related task-based fMRI study in which participants were explicitly instructed to use cognitive reappraisal to up- and down-regulate emotional responses to visual stimuli (film/video clips). It reports within-task contrasts for emotion regulation (Increase + Decrease vs Look-Sports and other relevant contrasts) and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with reported activations and tables/coordinates. Sample characteristics are provided (healthy adult participants). The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). No exclusion criteria apply: this is empirical task-fMRI with whole-brain task activation maps, not ROI-only, connectivity-only, resting-state-only, or non-empirical, and it is not an empathy/perspective-taking study without regulation instructions. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I11 and is eligible for inclusion.

This study includes two instructed volitional reappraisal tasks (Task 4: distancing; Task 5: positive reinterpretation) that directly instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses. Task 5 uses visual picture stimuli (negative/positive/neutral images); Task 4 uses visual symbols. The paper reports within-task contrasts of regulation (R > NR) and unregulated viewing (e.g., Neg/NR > Neu/NR), and conducted group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with thresholded activation maps. Participants are healthy human adults. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not empathy-only). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment using visual emotional stimuli (computer-generated faces) and reports within-task contrasts that index emotional discrimination (threatening > not threatening). It includes a suitable participant sample (healthy adults) and reports group-level voxelwise analyses with coordinates (voxelwise results and Tables 2/3), meeting whole-brain reporting requirements. Although no emotion-regulation instruction was given, the review objective and inclusion criterion I9 explicitly allow unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., emotion > baseline), which this study provides. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore the paper qualifies for inclusion under the meta-analysis criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructed cognitive reappraisal (distancing) during presentation of visual negative and neutral pictures (Emotional Picture Set). The paper reports within-task contrasts (RegulateNeg vs WatchNeg; WatchNeg vs WatchNeu), whole-brain group-level analyses with MNI peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction, and psychophysiological interaction (PPI) connectivity analyses. The sample is healthy adult participants and results for the task are reported at the group level. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (whole-brain maps are reported; this is not a review, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or empathy task without emotion regulation). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual (video) stimuli in obesity and control groups and reports within-task condition comparisons of dynamic connectivity; however it does not instruct participants to perform an emotion regulation strategy (participants were instructed only to watch attentively), and it does not report any group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps or peak coordinates. Thus it fails inclusion criteria I6 (no instructed regulation) and I10 (no whole-brain task activation maps). Additionally, the paper reports only ROI-based dynamic functional connectivity and Granger causality analyses without accompanying whole-brain task activation results, meeting exclusion criteria E4 and E5. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: videos), I8 (sample includes clinical and control groups), and I9 (within-task condition comparisons reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 and I10. Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on task-evoked whole-brain activation contrasts of instructed emotion regulation.

Exclusion rationale: E4 applies (study reports main task activation using small-volume-corrected/amygdala ROI results without a reported group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map). Inclusion met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample qualifies: healthy adults), I9 (reports an unregulated viewing/elicitation contrast: sad vs neutral). Inclusion NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy — task is mood induction/script-driven recall, not reappraisal or other instructed regulation), I7 (stimuli are script-driven imagery and music, not visual emotional images; thus regulated/elicited stimuli are non-visual), I10 (no clear whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map reported — primary activation was assessed with SVC). Because at least one required inclusion criterion (I6 and I7 and I10) is not satisfied and an exclusion criterion (E4) is met, the study is excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructed cognitive reappraisal (ER task) using visual IAPS images, reporting within-task contrasts (Reappraise > Look; Reappraise > implicit baseline) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates (e.g., left IFG -45,21,18). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed cognitive reappraisal (distancing) during stimulus presentation and included passive viewing, using visual IAPS images. It reports within-task regulation contrasts and long-term passive-viewing contrasts, presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and FWE correction, and provides full methods, results, and discussion. Sample is healthy adult participants. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Complete task-based fMRI study instructing cognitive reappraisal; regulation occurred during viewing of neutral faces (visual stimuli). Reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > look), whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with tables/figures and coordinates. Sample and methods are described in full text. Thus it meets all meta-analysis inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study (concurrent EEG/fMRI) that instructs emotion regulation using cognitive reappraisal (cue ‘decrease’), with visual stimuli (IAPS images). Group-level fMRI GLM maps (NEU, NEG, NER) are reported with cluster correction and used to define ROIs, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. The paper reports within-task contrasts and condition-specific effects and provides full methods, results, and discussion. Sample includes healthy adult participants and group-level results are presented. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study using a visual emotional stimulus (a film clip) and an instructed regulation-style task (structured prompts to elaborate on an induced sad mood). The analysis includes within-task contrasts (elaboration vs. baseline/fixation), whole-brain, group-level voxelwise comparisons with thresholding and reported coordinates, and results are reported in text/tables. Participants are children (eligible sample). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is empirical, reports whole-brain task activation (not only ROI or connectivity), and includes within-task effects. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs a cognitive reappraisal strategy (Regulate vs Attend) to modulate responses to investment outcomes. The regulated stimuli are visual (market price displays/graphical feedback) that evoke emotional responses (regret/loss aversion) targeted by regulation. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing Regulate and Attend (behavioral and fMRI), and whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates in standard space. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal/emotional reappraisal strategies (emotion regulation) during a visual social-scenes task and during neurofeedback. Visual stimuli (social scenes images) were used. The sample (adolescent females) is eligible. The paper reports within-task activation contrasts (e.g., appraisal > fixation, reappraisal > fixation, reappraisal > appraisal) used as localizer contrasts, and describes group-level ROI probability maps with MNI coordinates for PFC and amygdala centers, indicating whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results in standard space. Thus all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met. No exclusion criteria are met.

This full-text reports an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (distancing/reinterpretation) using visual negative images (IAPS), includes clinical (MDD, BPD) and healthy control groups with group-level results reported separately, presents within-task contrasts related to regulation (Regulate>Maintain, Maintain>Observe), and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster/peak coordinates (TFCE, MNI). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary material is referenced but not required for inclusion. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional images and reports whole-brain, group-level within-task contrasts contrasting negative vs. neutral images with peak coordinates. Although the task required emotion identification rather than an instructed emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal/other regulation instruction), the review objective and inclusion criterion I9 permit unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., emotion > neutral). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and provides SPM whole-brain results and coordinates. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for inclusion as an unregulated viewing task-based fMRI study.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use a cognitive reappraisal (distancing) strategy while viewing visual stimuli (IAPS and photographs). Sample includes ages 6–23. Within-task contrasts (Reappraisal/Negative > Reactivity/Negative and related contrasts) are reported, and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described with peak coordinates and tables. The paper also reports PPI connectivity analyses but not exclusively, and whole-brain activation maps and tables are provided. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables).

Full text reviewed and excluded because the emotional stimuli used are monetary gambles and outcomes (financial decision-making), not visual emotional stimuli such as static images or film/video. Therefore inclusion criterion I7 (emotional stimuli are VISUAL images or video) is not met. The study does satisfy: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation via reappraisal/perspective-taking), I8 (appropriate sample reporting), I9 (reports within-task regulation and viewing contrasts), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), and I11 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to upregulate positive-social emotions via self-referential imagination (an instructed regulation strategy). Stimuli are visual (IAPS/NAPS/GAPED photographs). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., upregulate positive > viewing neutral) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with FWE correction and coordinate reporting. All inclusion criteria relevant to the review are satisfied, and none of the exclusion criteria apply (the study reports whole-brain activation results in addition to DCM connectivity analyses). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (increase, decrease, maintain) while recalling previously encoded IAPS images. The emotional stimuli are visual (IAPS pictures encoded pre-scan), the sample is healthy young adults, and the paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., decrease>maintain, increase>maintain) and post-scan recognition. Analyses include group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistics normalized to MNI space with reported peak coordinates and tables; SVC was used for amygdala but whole-brain results are present. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to perform attention-shifting and an appraisal (like/dislike) task that functions as an instructed emotion-appraisal strategy. Stimuli are visual static composite images of faces and scenes. The paper reports within-task contrasts directly related to regulation (like/dislike – male/female; indoor/outdoor – male/female) and implicit emotion processing (male/female – face-only). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates (MNI) and FWE thresholds. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based, within-subject fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (film clips) and reports task-evoked whole-brain group analyses (GLM) with cluster results and coordinates (Tables/Figures). Although the study did not instruct an explicit regulation strategy (it probed implicit regulation), it reports unregulated viewing contrasts (negative vs neutral) and stimulation-related modulation of emotion-related activation, which fits the review objective to include studies that either instruct regulation or involve viewing without regulating. Sample and analyses meet eligibility: participants scanned during an emotion-induction task, visual stimuli (videos), whole-brain group results, and reported contrasts relevant to emotion processing. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, non-empirical) are violated.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of visual emotional stimuli that tests relationships among inattention, brain activity, and perceived stress, it does NOT meet the requirement that an emotion regulation strategy was instructed (I6). The task involved implicit processing (matching negative faces vs shapes) with no instruction to regulate; therefore there is no within-task instructed reappraisal contrast (e.g., “reappraise > look”). While the study provides a within-task unregulated viewing contrast (Match Faces > Match Shapes) and subject-level whole-brain maps used for pattern expression analyses, it does not report a traditional group-level whole-brain task-evoked regulation contrast with peak coordinates as required (I10 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (contains an unregulated viewing contrast). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) appear to be met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (positive and minimizing reappraisal) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The sample is healthy adults, and the paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., positive reappraisal > natural response; minimizing reappraisal > natural response) and parametric analyses. Group-level whole-brain analyses and peak coordinates are reported (whole-brain contrasts, SVC and cluster-corrected results, and reported peaks in MNI space). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study in adolescents that includes both an instructed explicit emotion-regulation task (Perspective Task: ‘Far’ distancing/reappraisal vs ‘Close’) and an implicit regulation task (emotional N-Back). Stimuli are visual (faces, IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts indexing regulation and viewing (e.g., Far[Neg-Neu] > Close[Neg-Neu], 2-Back vs 0-Back contrasts) and describes whole-brain analyses (reported in supplement), satisfying the requirement for group-level whole-brain task activation maps. A clinical group (internalizing disorders) and a comparison group are reported separately. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; includes within-task effects). Full text is complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI experiment in healthy adults that instructed participants to use emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and distraction) while viewing negative and neutral visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., view NEG – reappraise; view NEG – distract) and provides peak coordinates in standard MNI space. Although primary ROI/SVC results are emphasized, the manuscript states complementary whole-brain exploratory analyses are provided in the supplementary material (with coordinates), satisfying the requirement for group-level whole-brain task activation reporting. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the article is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of passive viewing of emotional faces (meets I5). Stimuli are visual (I7), samples include patients and controls reported separately (I8), and the paper reports unregulated viewing contrasts (negative faces > baseline) with coordinates (I9, I11). However, no instructed emotion-regulation task was used (I6 not met). Critically, all task-evoked activation analyses were performed within an anatomical mask (bilateral amygdala and prefrontal cortex) rather than as an unrestricted whole-brain voxelwise task activation map; the paper therefore reports only ROI/mask-limited voxelwise results with no accompanying whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (meets exclusion E4). Also I10 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map) is not satisfied. Therefore the study must be excluded per E4. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (I6) using visual stimuli (IAPS images; I7). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reapp Neg vs Look Neg) and behavioral reappraisal success (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported with MNI peak coordinates and cluster thresholds (I10, I11). Participant sample information is provided (I8). Methods, results and discussion are present in the full text (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria apply.

Full text reports an empirical, task-based fMRI study using an instructed cognitive reappraisal paradigm (titles prompting reinterpretation) with visual IAPS stimuli. The methods describe first-level within-subject contrasts (IAPS2–IAPS1) identifying upward and downward reappraisal, and second-level, group-level voxelwise t tests comparing high- and low-Mach groups. Results list activation clusters across the brain (Table/Fig references and peak coordinates implied) and report SPM-based processing; thus whole-brain, group-level task activation maps are available. All inclusion criteria for the review are satisfied (task-based fMRI; instructed emotion regulation—reappraisal; visual stimuli; acceptable sample; within-task regulation contrasts; whole-brain evidence; reporting in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI/SVC results, only connectivity, non-empirical, or only between-group contrasts without within-task effects) are met. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore include in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) while participants view visual emotional images (IAPS and internet photos). It reports within-task contrasts comparing regulation conditions (e.g., REAP > ESUP, NAT vs REAP) and unregulated viewing, and presents group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space and statistical thresholds. Sample and methods are appropriate and full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-visual stimuli, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and distraction) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). Sample: healthy volunteers. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (reappraisal > view, distraction > view, reappraisal vs distraction) and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with FDR-corrected thresholds and coordinate tables; functional connectivity (PPI) is also reported but task activations are primary. Full article includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly addresses the review objective. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation-like task — affect labeling — was used), I7 (visual stimuli: emotional face images), I8 (eligible participant sample reported), I9 (within-task contrast affect label > gender label reported), I10 (group-level, whole-brain analysis used to identify functional peaks for ROIs), I11 (peaks/ROIs and contrasts are described and reported in figures/tables). Whole-brain group-level contrasts (AL–GL) were used to define functional peaks and extract percent signal change for predictive analyses, indicating standard-space voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Based on these factors, the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study instructing emotion-regulation strategies (mindfulness and a CBT-style “reality checking” cognitive reappraisal) applied during anticipation and perception of negative/unknown visual IAPS pictures. The study reports within-task contrasts (e.g. exp ng>nt, per ng>nt), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster thresholds and coordinates, plus ROI results. Sample comprises healthy adult participants with between-group comparisons but also within-task effects. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This study is a resting-state fMRI investigation of intrinsic functional connectivity in mTBI; it does not include any task-based emotion regulation paradigm or visual emotional stimuli, nor does it report within-task contrasts or whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Therefore it does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria requiring task-based fMRI with instructed emotion regulation and visual stimuli. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (increase, decrease, maintain) while participants view visual IAPS pictures. It reports within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation (e.g. negative>neutral, increase>maintain, decrease>maintain) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI peak coordinates and tables. The sample comprises healthy adult participants and methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study instructing emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) while participants viewed visual negative images (Chinese Affective Picture System). It reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > watch; suppress > watch; watch-negative > watch-neutral) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported activations/coordinates; small-volume amygdala analyses supplement but whole-brain results are present. Sample and stimuli meet inclusion, and the full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects). Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an original, task-based fMRI experiment that instructs cognitive reappraisal (decrease) versus look conditions using visual stimuli (IAPS and child-appropriate images). The sample spans ages 10–22 (children, adolescents, young adults). Behavioral contrasts (look negative > look neutral; decrease negative > look negative) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise fMRI analyses are reported with thresholding and peak coordinates/tables, and figures illustrate activation maps. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task contrasts and whole-brain maps). Therefore the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion requirements.

This is a task-based fMRI study (n=42) that instructs emotion-regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) during anticipation (cue) and stimulus (target) phases using visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g. Target Reappraisal > Target Appraise; Cue Suppression > Cue Reappraisal) and presents group-level whole-brain, FWE-corrected voxelwise results with MNI coordinates and tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual stimuli (faces), an eligible sample (healthy adults), and reports whole-brain group-level task activation results (satisfies I5, I7, I8, I10, I11). However, the task does not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses (e.g., reappraise, suppress, or otherwise down-/up-regulate emotion). Instead, it is a cognitive control/response-inhibition task (cue to report the ‘actual’ or ‘opposite’ emotion) and examines correlations with self-reported habitual regulation. Therefore it does NOT meet I6 (an instructed emotion regulation strategy) and does not provide within-task contrasts that clearly reflect an instructed emotion-regulation manipulation (I9 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that instructed a mindfulness emotion-regulation strategy during anticipation and viewing of emotional visual stimuli (IAPS). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (negative>neutral; unknown>neutral), group-level whole-brain random-effects comparisons with coordinates and cluster tables, and ROI analyses. It therefore satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I5); instructed emotion regulation (mindfulness) during expectation and stimulus (I6); visual static images as stimuli (I7); eligible sample (healthy adults) (I8); within-task contrasts reported (I9); group-level whole-brain maps with coordinates (I10); and adequate reporting in tables/figures (I11). The full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Regulate) and includes an unregulated viewing/maintenance condition (Maintain and Observe) using visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (Maintain>Observe; Regulate>Maintain) and provides group-level activation results with peak coordinates (MNI) and one-sample activations used to generate masks; PPI analyses also used whole-brain masking. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs cognitive emotion regulation (self-distancing), using visual negative images (IAPS). The paper reports within-task contrasts (CER vs NoCER; parametric aPE regressors) and describes whole-brain GLM preprocessing and voxelwise analyses (including coordinate-based ROI center x=26,y=6,z=-8 and supplementary aPE-related activation results), satisfying whole-brain evidence. Sample and stimulus criteria are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study is a task-based fMRI experiment with visual stimuli (food images) and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain analyses, but it does not include an instructed emotion regulation strategy. Specifically: (a) Exclusion criteria met: none. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task contrasts/unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (reports whole-brain results), I11 (results reported in text/tables). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instruction to regulate emotion/cognitive reappraisal or other instructed regulation). The meta-analysis requires studies that include instructed emotion regulation tasks (or else meet all listed inclusion criteria); because this study manipulated taste (an incidental, non-instructed intervention) rather than instructing participants to reappraise or otherwise regulate their emotional responses, it does not satisfy I6 and therefore must be excluded. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and distraction) during presentation of visual IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts and univariate GLM results (age-by-condition interactions), MVPA searchlight and ROI analyses, and whole-brain voxelwise thresholding with reported peak regions in MNI space. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an affect-labeling emotion regulation task (Label > Observe contrasts), with visual stimuli (static face photographs). Participants are adolescent females. Analyses include within-task regulation contrasts (Label>Observe for negative and positive), whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses, and reported PPI (task-related) whole-brain regression results (clusters reported in tables/figures). Affect labeling is an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (implicit regulation), satisfying the review’s allowed adjacent strategies. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only without task maps, not non-empirical). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I11 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly instructs cognitive emotion regulation (reappraisal: increase, decrease, look) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (increase > look, look > decrease, increase > decrease), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps with peak coordinates in standard space (MNI/ICBM) and tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual facial stimuli in healthy participants and reports within-task contrasts (e.g. Sad>Shape, Anger>Shape), so it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), and I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrasts).
