The study should be excluded because the emotional stimuli used are personalized trauma/stressful words (word/sentence stimuli), which the review's eligibility criteria explicitly exclude (I7 not met). The manuscript otherwise meets multiple inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5), includes a participant sample with separate patient and control groups (I8), reports within-task regulation contrasts (regulate vs view) (I9), and provides whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses with FDR-corrected results and reported coordinates (I10, I11). The regulation manipulation is neurofeedback-based (instructed downregulation of PCC), which may satisfy an instruction-to-regulate requirement (I6) ambiguously, but exclusion is driven by I7. No exclusion criteria E3–E7 apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study meets several inclusion criteria (I5: task-based fMRI; I6: instructed emotion regulation ‘dampen negative’; I7: visual stimuli (IAPS images); I8: clinical and control samples reported separately; I9: within-task contrasts/conditions reported). However, the analyses are ROI/parcellation-based (400 cortical parcels + subcortical ROIs) rather than group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with peak coordinates in standard space. The paper does not report voxelwise maps or peak coordinates. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ROI-based results with no accompanying whole-brain voxelwise analysis) and fails to meet inclusion criteria I10 (whole-brain voxelwise map with peak coordinates) and I11 (no coordinate/voxelwise results reported). Thus it must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (faces) with patient and control groups, reporting whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (happy>neutral, sad>neutral). However, the fMRI task is an emotion-matching/viewing task without any instructed emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other regulation instructions). Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 (requires an instructed emotion-regulation task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered by the provided full text. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation using visual images in patient and control groups (meets I5, I6, I7, I8). However, the manuscript does not report conventional within-task activation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > view or watch negative > neutral) nor present a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map with peak coordinates in standard space. Instead the fMRI analyses focus on global signal correlation/topography (region-parcellation GSCORR) and its association with behavioral ratings. Therefore it does not provide the required within-task contrasts or voxelwise activation coordinates for inclusion. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports connectivity/global-signal correlation style analyses without a whole-brain task activation map) and E6 (no within-group task activation contrasts reported). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I9 (no standard within-task contrast reported), I10 (no voxelwise group-level activation map with peak coordinates), (hence I11 not satisfied). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise vs attend) using visual stimuli (IAPS and alcohol photographs). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (reappraise > attend) and unregulated viewing contrasts (attend emotion > attend neutral), and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates and thresholding. Both patient (ADP) and control (HC) groups are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This study used a task-based fMRI paradigm (emotional face gender-labeling) but did not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy; analyses focused on whole-brain connectivity (ICD) and seed-based connectivity during the task rather than reporting task-evoked within-task activation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look or emotion > baseline) or whole-brain task-activation maps with peak coordinates. Therefore it does not meet key inclusion criteria requiring an emotion-regulation instruction or at minimum a within-task unregulated viewing contrast and a task-evoked whole-brain activation map. Exclusion criteria for connectivity-only/task-without-activation results are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual IAPS pictures in a Hariri picture-matching task (meets I5 and I7). It reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (negative vs. neutral; Neg–Neu) with group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and peak coordinates, and extracts βs from significant clusters (meets I9, I10, I11). Sample includes healthy adult participants with group results reported (meets I8). Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction was given (I6 not met), the review objective explicitly allows studies that involve viewing without regulation; thus the reported unregulated whole-brain contrast qualifies. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study with an instructed regulation block (‘‘imagine’’ calming imagery) and visual stimuli (colored CS squares). It reports within-task contrasts (threat vs. safe; contrast of threat-watching with vs. without suppression priming) and uses a healthy college sample. However, all reported neural results are ROI-based (amygdala percent signal change and correlations); the paper does not report any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) activation maps or peak coordinates. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I10 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain analysis). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise vs React) across socio-emotional tasks (looming faces, video clips of social criticism, and written negative self-beliefs). It includes visual stimuli (photos of faces and video clips; beliefs are presented as written sentences but the study also uses clear visual image/video stimuli), reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > React; one-sample and between-group tests), and provides whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses with cluster-corrected results and peak coordinates. Sample includes a clinical SAD group and healthy controls reported separately. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-without-regulation) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual face stimuli and reports unregulated viewing contrasts (sad vs neutral), but it does not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses (no reappraisal/other instructed regulation). Furthermore, the reported analyses focus on predefined ROIs and network-averaged responses rather than providing a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation map with peak coordinates. Therefore it fails the key inclusion criteria I6 (instructed emotion regulation) and I10 (whole-brain voxelwise results) and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ROI/network-based results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrast). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed regulation), I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise maps). Exclusion criteria met: E4. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (Emotion Regulation Task) using visual IAPS images in healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise vs Maintain and related contrasts), behavioral within-group regulation effects, and voxelwise results with peak coordinates (e.g., left amygdala −28,4,−18; dlPFC peaks) and whole-brain thresholds, satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not purely ROI-only, not only connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and is INCLUDED.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (and savoring) of visual stimuli (drug, food, neutral images). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (e.g., reappraise drug > look drug) and unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., look drug > look neutral/food). Analyses are voxelwise/whole-brain using FSL FLAME with cluster thresholds and whole-brain results reported (with supplementary material referenced), satisfying whole-brain map reporting. Sample includes clinical groups (HUD/CUD) and both sexes with within-subject menstrual phase comparisons. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs emotion regulation (regulate vs view conditions; I6), uses visual stimuli (IAPS pictures; I7), includes participant groups with results reported separately (patients with FMS, MDD, and healthy controls; I8), and reports within-task regulation-related contrasts (REG > VIEW and related baseline vs transfer contrasts; I9). Group-level second-level analyses were performed and exploratory whole-brain analyses are described (with MNI coordinates reported for peaks and SI referenced), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps (I10) and acceptable reporting formats (I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is empirical with original fMRI data and does not report only ROI/partial-coverage results or only connectivity/between-group-only contrasts, nor is it an empathy/perspective-taking-only task. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS/photographs) and an instructed task that includes emotion labeling (an antecedent-focused/instructed cognitive strategy shown to reduce amygdala reactivity), satisfying the review’s emotion-regulation task requirement. The paper reports within-task contrasts (self/positive, label/positive, etc. vs control) and group-level voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and whole-brain results/tables. Sample includes healthy adult participants. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI-only results, only connectivity, non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11 are met and the study should be INCLUDED.

This study is excluded because it reports only ROI-based task analyses (VmPFC, amygdala, ventral striatum) and does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or peak coordinates in standard space. Exclusion criterion met: E4 (ONLY ROI results/no whole-brain analysis). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual static image stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrast: stress > neutral). Inclusion criteria not met: I10 (no whole-brain evidence/voxelwise maps reported). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, discussion; exclusion is based on analytic reporting.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study with instructed cognitive reappraisal and reports within-task regulation contrasts and whole-brain group analyses, it must be excluded because the regulated stimuli are text-based math problems and analogies (visual words/numeric stimuli). The review’s I7 criterion excludes studies whose regulated stimuli are word or sentence stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation — cognitive reappraisal), I8 (eligible sample: adolescents and young adults), I9 (reports within-task reappraise > look contrasts), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I11 (results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (stimuli are word/sentence stimuli, which are excluded). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This full-text reports an original task-based fMRI study that directly instructs cognitive reappraisal (regulation phase: ‘reappraise’ vs ‘attend’), using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The paper includes both regulation contrasts (Reappraisal versus Attend Negative) and unregulated viewing contrasts (View Negative versus View Neutral). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses are reported with MNI peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction; small-volume correction for the amygdala is additionally described but whole-brain results are present and reported. The sample comprises UHR participants and matched healthy controls with separate within-group and between-group analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This task-based fMRI study used visual emotional face stimuli and reports unregulated viewing contrasts (emotion > crosshair) and ROI (left amygdala) voxel-wise results associated with clinical changes. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—faces), I8 (sample includes adolescents/young adults), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts/condition-related BOLD changes), and I11 (results described in text/figures). However, the fMRI task did not instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy during scanning (I6 not met). Critically, the reported imaging results are limited to an a priori ROI with small volume correction (left amygdala); no whole-brain task-activation peak coordinates or surviving whole-brain group-level activation map are provided (I10 not met). This violates exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI/SVC results reported with no accompanying whole-brain analysis results). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal (CRA) during the Cyberball task; visual stimuli (animated avatars/ball-tossing) were used. The paper reports within-task contrasts (EXC > INC; VIEW vs CRA; interaction contrasts examining regulation effects) and second-level random-effects voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space (reported throughout results and tables, with FWE-corrected peaks). Methods describe whole-brain preprocessing and GLM; ROI/SVC analyses were also used but not exclusively. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it is a resting-state seed-based functional connectivity study and does not include any task-based emotion regulation paradigm. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without any task-evoked whole-brain activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample criteria: participants of qualifying ages/groups). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli; resting-state), I9 (no within-task regulation or viewing contrasts reported), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate emotion (reappraise/decrease vs look), using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). Sample is healthy young adults. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (decrease negative > look negative and look negative > look neutral) and ROI and whole-brain group-level random-effects analyses with tables/figures and peak coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not empathy-without-regulation). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so completeness is adequate.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (I7; IAPS images), with an eligible sample (adults; ADHD and controls reported separately) (I8). The paper reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (negative > neutral) (I9) and presents whole-brain permutation-based analyses and corrected activation maps/figures (I10, I11). However, the study did NOT instruct participants to use an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraise/distancing/acceptance instruction); participants simply viewed emotional images, so inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy) is not met. No exclusion criteria were triggered (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or empathy-perspective-only design). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I6 while meeting other inclusion criteria.

Excluded because the study does not meet all inclusion criteria and meets an exclusion criterion. Inclusion met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: angry/fearful faces), I8 (sample eligible), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrast: angry/fearful faces vs shapes). Inclusion not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation – task was face-matching with no reappraisal/other regulation instructions), I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps or reported peak coordinates; analyses focused on ROI extractions), I11 (not applicable because no whole-brain results reported). Exclusion met: E4 (reports only ROI-based analyses/extractions with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Full text appears complete. Given failure to meet I6 and I10 and presence of E4, exclude.

Full-text is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion regulation paradigm (attend vs reduce-negative, enhance-positive) with visual IAPS stimuli. The study reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (LME), with cluster results/maps reported. Sample includes patient and control groups. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply; the paper is empirical, reports whole-brain activation (not only ROI or connectivity), and includes within-task effects. Full text is complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (Increase/Decrease) during presentation of visual stimuli (static angry faces). It reports within-task contrasts (Decrease vs Observe-angry, Increase vs Observe-angry, Observe-angry > Observe-neutral) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and tables. Sample comprises healthy adult participants and resting-state subset; task-based results are reported for the full sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I11) and none of the exclusion criteria apply (E3–E7).

This study is excluded because it is not a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed emotion regulation of visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample qualifies: children/adolescents). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study; uses structural MRI brain-age prediction), I6 (no fMRI emotion regulation task or instructed regulation), I7 (no emotion-eliciting VISUAL stimuli presented as part of an fMRI task), I9 (no within-task regulation contrasts reported such as reappraise>look), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps/peak coordinates). No exclusion criteria from the review’s list apply (e.g., paper is empirical and reports original data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not meet the core task-based fMRI and task-contrast requirements and is excluded.

Full article text contains methods, results, and discussion. This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal of drug images and savoring of food images). Stimuli are visual static images. Participant groups (heroin use disorder and healthy controls) are reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraise drug>look drug; savor food>look food) and unregulated viewing contrasts (look drug>look neutral; look drug>look food). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, with cluster thresholds and peak coordinates reported in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (self-focused distancing) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation (Decrease > LookNeg; LookNeg > LookNeu) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates, tables, and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and instructions explicitly required regulation).

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (face distracters) during an emotional-distracter n-back task. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level SPM12 analyses with coordinates and cluster tables and examines contrasts across emotional (fear/happy/neutral) distracter conditions, thus providing within-task emotional (unregulated) condition effects appropriate for the review’s scope (studies that regulate or view visual emotional stimuli). The sample includes clinical (BD-COBY) and healthy control groups with results reported separately. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion with whole-brain coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11 are met. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal-style instructions: “pretend it’s fake”/“pretend it’s right in front of you”), using visual disgust-inducing images (IAPS + child-appropriate photos). The sample (children/adolescents) is acceptable. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (decrease-gross > look-gross, increase-gross > look-gross) and an unregulated viewing contrast (look-gross > look-neutral). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster thresholds and Talairach-normalized results (including reported coordinates for mPFC), satisfying requirements for spatially standardized peak reporting. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not review-only, not ROI-only, includes task activation maps, not solely connectivity or between-group-only, not an empathy-only paradigm).

This study uses resting-state fMRI and predictive modeling of methamphetamine abstinence outcomes; it does not employ a task-based fMRI paradigm or any instructed emotion regulation strategy. Exclusion criterion E5 applies (reports only resting-state analyses without any whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criterion I8 is met (sample: human participants, clinical population with controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli/task), I9 (no within-task regulation or viewing contrasts), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study is excluded from the emotion regulation fMRI meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal strategies (Decrease Negative, Increase Positive) while viewing standardized visual emotional stimuli (IAPS and supplementary images). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation (Decrease Negative vs Look Negative; Increase Positive vs Look Negative) at the group level, using voxelwise analyses (baseline functional localizer with voxelwise contrast thresholding, cluster correction) in standard (Talairach) space and reports cluster locations/coordinates in figures/tables. Sample characteristics are acceptable (human participants; results reported for the group). The full text includes methods, results and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (reappraisal and acceptance) and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain group-level maps; however, the emotional stimuli are participant-generated negative self-beliefs presented as text (one-line sentences). Inclusion criterion I7 requires visual emotional stimuli such as images or film and explicitly excludes studies whose regulated stimuli are word/sentence stimuli. Therefore the study does not meet I7 and must be excluded.

The full text describes a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly instructed emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and suppression) during viewing of visual emotional stimuli (I6, I7). The sample (healthy adults, multi-center) meets sample inclusion (I8). Reported within-task contrasts include View Negative > View Neutral and Reappraise > Attend Negative and Suppress > Attend Negative, satisfying the requirement for within-task regulation and unregulated viewing contrasts (I9). Analyses include group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistics with reported cluster- and voxelwise results and tables/figures (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text is complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). Adult patient and control groups are reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (EI>ER, ER>EI, deactivation during ER, etc.) and presents whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses with MNI coordinates and cluster thresholds (Z>3.1, corrected p<0.05). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli and an instructed emotion-regulation-like manipulation (redirecting attention during an emotional face n-back), with within-task contrasts and adolescent clinical and control groups reported. However, all reported neuroimaging results are ROI-based (activity and seed-based PPI between anatomically defined ROIs) and the paper does not present any group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps or peak coordinates in standard space. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I10 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ROI results / no whole-brain analysis). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to regulate emotional responses (suppress vs. maintain) while viewing visual negative and neutral images. The methods report within-task contrasts (e.g., suppressing emotions vs. looking at negative pictures) and voxel-wise whole-brain group analyses with peak coordinates and small-volume corrections; results include whole-brain activation and connectivity findings. The sample (adult shift workers and controls) is appropriate, and the article contains full introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise vs attend) using visual stimuli (IAPS and alcohol images). Participant groups include AUD patients and healthy controls with group-specific analyses. The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > attend; attend emotion > attend neutral) and conducts second-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses in SPM with results reported at a whole-brain FWE-corrected threshold; the text further references peak voxels and extracted beta weights, indicating standard-space peak-based whole-brain reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) with an eligible participant sample (I8), reports within-task contrasts for emotional valence conditions (IntPos/IntNeg etc) and whole-brain group-level results with coordinates/cluster reporting (I9,I10). However it fails key inclusion criteria: (I6) no instructed emotion-regulation strategy (participants evaluated their internal state rather than being instructed to reappraise, distance, accept, or otherwise regulate their emotional response); and (I7) the emotional stimuli are word adjectives (verbal/word stimuli), not visual images or film clips, and the review explicitly excludes studies whose regulated stimuli are words/sentences. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal during presentation of visual spider photographs, reports within-task regulation contrasts (regulate vs. watch), and includes whole-brain group-level random-effects GLM analyses (with thresholding and supplementary tables/figures). Sample comprises clinical spider-phobic participants (adults) with a control group; follow-up behavioral outcomes are reported. All inclusion criteria relevant to the review are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

This is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs emotion regulation (reappraise vs. maintain) using visual negative images in healthy participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > maintain, maintain > baseline, etc.) and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates and cluster statistics in standard (MNI) space. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (emotional faces) and reports within-task contrasts (fearful>scrambled, angry>scrambled, neutral>scrambled) and whole-brain group-level results with coordinates. Participants include clinical (PTSD+personality disorder) and matched controls. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I7, I8, I9, I10 and I11. However, the fMRI task is an emotional face matching task with no instruction to regulate emotion (no cognitive reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other instructed regulation during anticipation or stimulus). Thus it does NOT meet I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met, the study is excluded for failing I6 (no instructed emotion regulation). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (faces) and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain, voxelwise results with MNI coordinates. Although the task is an emotional conflict/processing task without an instruction to explicitly regulate emotions (I6 not met), the study reports unregulated emotion-related task contrasts (e.g., trial and emotion effects; incongruent vs. congruent; emotion main effects), satisfying the allowed ‘view without regulating’ arm of the review. Whole-brain group-level analyses with peak coordinates are provided, and the sample is appropriate. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-task effects are reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus the study meets the meta-analysis objective and qualifies for inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs explicit emotion regulation strategies (Compassion meditation and Reappraisal) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (film clips). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Compassion > Watch-Negative; Reappraisal > Watch-Negative) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with corrected inference (cluster-level FWE) and reported tables/figures. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal/distancing) while viewing visual stimuli (validated photographs). It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., regulate/Far vs baseline and comparisons to Look), includes behavioral ratings, and describes univariate GLM analyses (results reported in the Supplement), indicating group-level task-evoked analyses. The paper contains full methods, results, and discussion (not merely title/abstract), and the Supplement is noted to include univariate results, satisfying the allowance that whole-brain results may appear in supplementary materials. Thus all inclusion criteria for the review (I5–I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that includes instructed cognitive reappraisal (I6), uses visual stimuli (I7), reports an eligible sample including healthy controls (I8), and reports within-task regulation contrasts (Look vs Decrease; Match vs Label) (I9). However, the analyses are limited to ROI-based amygdala activation and PPI connectivity restricted to IFG anatomical masks; the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps or whole-brain peak coordinates (I10 not met). Therefore exclusion criterion E4 (reports ONLY region-of-interest or small-volume-corrected results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis) is met. No other exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Given the absence of whole-brain task-evoked maps (I10 unmet), the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (diminish/intensify/view) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., diminish > view, intensify > view) and unregulated viewing contrasts, and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FSL FLAME1, cluster-corrected) with reported activation results. Sample and methods are fully described, and ROI analyses are supplementary to whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, reports within-task effects, not an empathy-only task). Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed cognitive reappraisal (RETHINK) and included visual emotional stimuli (IAPS and breast-cancer-related pictures). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., IAPS-rethink > IAPS-watch, BC-rethink > BC-watch, BC-IAPS differential regulation) and unregulated viewing contrasts, and presents group-level whole-brain mixed-effects analyses (FLAME) with clusterwise results and MNI coordinates referenced. The sample includes patients and healthy controls with results reported separately. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly includes an instructed cognitive reappraisal condition (reappraise/negative) and an uninstructed viewing condition (look/negative vs look/neutral). Emotional stimuli are visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > look; look negative > look neutral) and trial-by-trial parametric analyses, and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with corrected thresholds and tables, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Participants are healthy adult humans. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not merely abstract/metadata). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I11 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This full-text study meets all review inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion-regulation paradigm (cognitive reappraisal: enhance/suppress) with visual stimuli (IAPS images). The analysis reports within-task contrasts (suppress vs. attend for negative stimuli) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space and cluster correction. The sample (MDD patients) is an eligible participant group. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion so appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-without-regulation) are met. Therefore include.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (attention-to-breath, a mindfulness/acceptance-like instruction) while participants view aversive visual images (IAPS). It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., ATB > PV, PV > ATB) and correlations with behavioral measures, and presents group-level whole-brain analyses in MNI space (with coordinates) alongside ROI and PPI analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I11) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the paper reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses and explicitly states that contrasts were analyzed using an ROI approach; no group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or peak coordinates in standard space are reported (violates exclusion E4). The study meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed cognitive reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli—IAPS images), I8 (acceptable sample—older adults; behavioral pilot includes younger adults), and I9 (reports within-task contrasts such as reinterpret > attend). It does NOT meet I10 (whole-brain evidence required). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This paper reports a task-based fMRI study with instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal and selective attention) using visual film stimuli in younger and older adult participants and provides within-task contrasts. However, the full text focuses on psychophysiological interaction (PPI) seed-based connectivity analyses and does not present a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map (activation contrasts were reported previously in another paper). According to the review’s exclusion criterion E5, studies that report ONLY seed-based/effective connectivity analyses without also reporting a whole-brain task activation map must be excluded. Therefore this article is excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation (I5) using visual stimuli (30-s video clips of play and separation; I7). The sample (mothers with and without IPV-PTSD) is an eligible participant group (I8). The analysis includes an unregulated viewing contrast (separation vs play) at the within-task level (I9). Authors report and describe a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analysis with cluster-extent correction (whole-brain 2nd-level analysis described in Methods and Results), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I10) and the acceptability of reporting in text/supplemental materials (I11). The task did not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not applicable), but the meta-analysis objective accepts unregulated viewing contrasts. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal versus a natural 'look' condition to regulate emotion. Visual stimuli (negative and neutral images) were used, and behavioral and within-task contrasts (reappraise > look for high- and low-intensity stimuli) are reported. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described and thresholded (AlphaSim) with tables/figures of peak coordinates and clusters reported; supplementary ROI analyses of the amygdala are included but do not replace the whole-brain results. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, enabling comprehensive assessment. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

The full text describes an empirical, task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal) paradigm (‘Think Objectively’ vs ‘Watch’) with visual IAPS images. The sample is a defined group of healthy participants (n=36 females). The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise negative > watch negative), second-level group analyses and functional connectivity results, and provides peak cluster information (e.g. L amygdala seed coordinate [−20, −4, −20], R IFG cluster k=1605) in tables/figures. Thus it meets the review’s task, stimulus, sample, contrast, and whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study using visual emotional film clips (EE) vs neutral (EN) with within-task contrasts (EE−EN) and group-level voxelwise SPM analyses reported. Stimuli are visual (film clips), sample is eligible, and the paper reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (emotion > neutral). Although participants were not instructed to use an explicit emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met), the meta-analysis scope accepts unregulated viewing contrasts (I9), so inclusion is appropriate. Full text appears complete.

This task-based fMRI study meets multiple inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I8, I9, I10, I11): it is a task fMRI study with instructed cognitive reappraisal (distancing), reports within-task reappraisal contrasts (R–NR), uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported coordinates, and includes full methods/results/discussion. However, it does NOT meet inclusion criterion I7: the emotional stimulus is anticipatory threat of shock (auditory cues/anticipation, eyes-closed), not visual stimuli (no pictures, faces, or film clips). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study is excluded solely for failing I7 (non-visual emotional stimuli).

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation that includes both instructed regulation (neurofeedback-driven downregulation of amygdala activity during fMRI-NF) and visual stimulus viewing tasks (backward masking; emotional faces in the emotional conflict task). It reports within-task regulation contrasts (NF vs rest; pre/post NF comparisons) and unregulated viewing (backward masking) effects, and presents whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates (e.g., amygdala x=23,y=-2,z=-17). Participants are healthy adults. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11). No exclusion criteria apply; full text appears complete.

Full text shows this is a task-based fMRI study with whole-brain analyses, but the fMRI task is a placebo analgesia pain paradigm (thermal stimuli on forearm) and does not instruct emotion regulation of visual stimuli. The cognitive reappraisal (CRA) task was administered in a separate lab session outside the scanner using visual pictures, but no in-scanner reappraisal instruction or reappraise>look contrast is reported. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria for this review: the fMRI task does not involve instructed emotion regulation (I6), the regulated stimuli in-scanner are non-visual/painful (I7), and no within-task emotion-regulation contrast from fMRI is reported (I9). Included: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample qualifies), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I11 (coordinates/tables described). No exclusion criteria from the list are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study (EFAT, ERT, SEAT) that explicitly instructs emotion regulation (Reappraise vs Maintain) and reports reappraisal-related contrasts. Stimuli are visual (IAPS images and emotional faces). Sample is healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation and unregulated viewing (Reappraise>Maintain, Maintain>baseline, Fearful>Happy). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are described and peak coordinates are provided (e.g., left DLPFC x=-40,y=12,z=28; left VLPFC x=-50,y=22,6), meeting whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI experiment that directly instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) and compares it to passive viewing and a placebo-based implicit regulation. Visual stimuli (disgust images) were used. The study reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Reappraisal (Disgust>Neutral), Placebo (Disgust>Neutral), Passive Viewing) in a repeated-measures design on 45 healthy adult women. The authors conducted whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA and follow-up contrasts) with FWE correction and also report ROI and PPI results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-task effects, not an empathy/perspective-taking-only paradigm). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) and includes an instructed reappraisal task in the scanner (participants practiced and performed an instructed reappraisal task) as well as an uninstructed image-viewing task. The paper reports within-task activation estimates for image viewing and uses these to predict regulation choices, and it presents group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates (whole-brain clusters reported). Sample and methods are fully described. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed emotion regulation task is included), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (acceptable sample), I9 (reports within-task contrasts/unregulated viewing), I10 (group-level whole-brain maps with coordinates), and I11 (results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Full text is complete. This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study of visual emotional face processing that reports whole-brain group-level results (faces > shapes) and correlations with individual differences in reappraisal. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample), I9 (reports an unregulated viewing contrast faces > shapes), I10 (whole-brain analyses with coordinates), I11 (results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (the study did NOT instruct an emotion regulation strategy; it assessed spontaneous/individual-difference reappraisal use via the ERQ rather than an instructed reappraisal manipulation). No exclusion criteria from E3–E7 apply. Because I6 is required, the study must be excluded from the set of instructed emotion-regulation fMRI contrasts.

This is a study protocol (non-empirical report) describing planned task-based fMRI in a randomized trial but it does not report original fMRI results or any within-task statistical contrasts or whole-brain coordinate maps. Exclusion criterion E3 applies (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data). Inclusion criteria met by the protocol: I5 (task-based fMRI planned), I7 (visual emotional stimuli — IAPS images), I8 (sample includes BPD patients and healthy controls). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy — task is passive viewing/rating), I9 (no reported within-task contrast results), I10 (no reported whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps/coordinates). Full text appears to be a complete protocol (background, methods, discussion) but lacks results, so mark fulltext_incomplete=true.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using an instructed emotion regulation task (participants instructed to "regulate the emotions evoked by the image") with visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (negative regulate > negative observe) and observes unregulated viewing contrasts. Whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses were performed and significant clusters are reported with MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected p-values. The sample (young adults) is eligible. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and the paper should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to regulate emotion (increase/attend/decrease) using cognitive reappraisal strategies while viewing visual IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts (increase>attend, decrease>attend), conducts whole-brain voxelwise ANOVAs with cluster results and tables/figures (group-level, standard-space coordinates), and includes an appropriate participant sample. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that included an explicit emotion regulation condition (Reframe) in the task design (I6), even though Reframe results are reported elsewhere. It reports unregulated viewing (React) contrasts versus a baseline/asterisks condition (React > Asterisks), satisfying the requirement for a within-task unregulated viewing contrast (I9). The stimuli include visual emotional probes (looming faces and dynamic video clips) meeting the visual-stimulus requirement (I7); although one task used text-based self-beliefs, the study also includes clearly visual tasks. The sample includes clinical (SAD) and healthy control groups reported separately (I8). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates/tables (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain results are presented (so not ROI-only or partial coverage), task activation maps and within-task contrasts are reported, and this is an empirical fMRI study. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based, longitudinal fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate negative affect using visual stimuli (IAPS/photographs). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation (Reappraisal vs Maintain; Reappraisal vs Baseline) and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with voxelwise thresholds, cluster tables, and peak coordinates, as well as ROI analyses for the amygdala. The sample and methods are fully described. All required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly tests emotion regulation (explicit Reappraise vs Maintain blocks) using visual stimuli (IAPS scenes for regulation; faces for free viewing). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraise > Maintain) and unregulated viewing contrasts (Surprise>Neutral, Fear>Neutral), and describes group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and Talairach peak coordinates (whole-brain results). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the review are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (distancing) during an event-related monetary incentive delay task. Participants regulated reward-related feelings elicited by visual cues (colored cues/targets) and outcomes; the paper reports within-task contrasts comparing distancing vs permitting (e.g., Distance > Permit) and other regulation-related contrasts. Group-level voxelwise results with MNI coordinates are reported for reappraisal activations and VST effects; whole-brain analyses are described alongside ROI-corrected tests. Sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. Although stimuli are monetary cues rather than affective pictures, they are visual and elicit emotional responses that subjects were instructed to regulate, so the study meets the review objective. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (angry/fear faces) and reports an unregulated viewing contrast (emotion > shape) with group-level whole-brain statistical maps and coordinates. Although no explicit emotion-regulation instructions were used, the meta-analysis objective includes studies that view stimuli without regulating; criterion I9 explicitly accepts unregulated viewing contrasts. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and provides whole-brain maps and coordinate tables. Therefore it meets the review requirements for visual-stimulus, task-based, within-task unregulated contrast and whole-brain reporting.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to apply emotion-regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal, suppression, up-regulation) while viewing visual stimuli (static high-calorie food pictures). The sample (healthy adult women) is eligible. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing regulation conditions (e.g., suppression vs. reappraisal, up-regulation vs. suppression) and presents a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise RFX ANOVA with Talairach normalization and corrected F-map used to define functional ROIs. Results and statistical tests (t, F values) are reported for these whole-brain-derived ROIs. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for emotion regulation fMRI studies with visual stimuli and whole-brain task activation reporting.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal: 'Think Objectively') using visual IAPS images in healthy adult participants, and it reports within-task contrasts and connectivity results. Inclusion met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation—reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli—IAPS images), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (within-task contrast related to regulation). However, the paper reports only seed-based functional connectivity (gPPI) / ROI coupling results and does not present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates in standard space in the full text (task activation maps/coordinates are not provided here; earlier related work contains such maps but not within this report). Therefore it violates I10 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only seed-based connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria not met: I10. Exclusion criteria met: E5.

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest ROI-based group analyses and does not present any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps with peak coordinates in standard space, violating E4. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (task includes an instructed emotion-regulation-like strategy — instructed attentional control/ignore emotional distractors), I7 (visual stimuli: static face images), I8 (sample includes patient and healthy control groups reported), I9 (within-task contrasts comparing emotional face vs no-face trials are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps/coordinates reported). Therefore excluded per E4.

This paper reports a task-based fMRI study (Cyberball) with visual animated stimuli, includes within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (observed inclusion > observed exclusion, observed exclusion > inclusion), and reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space. Sample (adolescents) meets the allowable participant criteria. Although no instructed emotion-regulation strategy (reappraisal, distancing, etc.) was used, the meta-analysis accepts unregulated viewing contrasts (I9), which this study provides. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical with original fMRI activation results, presents whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only), is not solely connectivity, and reports within-group task effects. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for unregulated viewing contrasts and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of youth using visual stimuli (faces, written family/non-family problem statements) and reports whole-brain voxel-wise task analyses and within-group effects. However, the study does not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses using a defined emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., cognitive reappraisal, distancing, acceptance). The emotion-processing task was implicit (gender identification) and the problem-solving task asked participants to imagine and solve problems but did not explicitly instruct up- or down-regulation of emotional responses. Thus Inclusion Criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation strategy) is not met. Additionally, while whole-brain voxel-wise analyses are reported, peak coordinates in standard space are not presented in the provided text, so I10 cannot be confirmed. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I10. No exclusion criteria (E3-E7) apply based on the provided full text. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that instructed participants to employ emotion regulation strategies (compassion vs. reappraisal) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (Negative–Neutral during Regulation; Post–Pre training), and conducts group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses with reported MNI peak coordinates (e.g., [24,26,-8] in right AI/OFC). All required inclusion criteria are met (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is a task-based, group-level fMRI study that instructed participants to perform cognitive reappraisal (increase/decrease) of visual IAPS images, with full reporting of within-task contrasts (e.g., decrease-negative > view-negative) and whole-brain voxelwise results in standard (MNI/Talairach) space. The full paper includes introduction, methods (fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, contrasts), results (tables/coordinates, figures), and discussion, and the analyses explicitly examine instructed emotion regulation vs. view conditions. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not a non-empirical paper, not exclusively between-group contrasts, and not an empathy/perspective-taking study without regulation instructions). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review and is suitable for inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual stimuli and an instructed implicit emotion-regulation paradigm (attend vs ignore fearful faces), reporting within-task contrasts and patient/control groups. However, all main reported analyses are ROI-based (a priori amygdala/insula ROIs and an exploratory larger ROI mask); the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I10 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (only ROI/partial-coverage results reported). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I10. Exclusion criteria met: E4. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This full text meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using instructed cognitive reappraisal (detach/reappraise) as the emotion-regulation strategy (I6), with visual stimuli (IAPS images) presented as static pictures (I7). The sample includes younger and older adult groups (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation and experience (e.g., Positive-Experience > Positive-Regulate; Negative-Regulate > Negative-Experience) and behavioral correlates (I9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates, cluster tables, and corrected thresholds (I10,I11). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria are violated. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: on-screen essay feedback and written prompts), I8 (eligible participant sample), I9 (reports within-task contrasts: feedback > baseline and provocation-focus > neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I11 (results described with cluster/coordinate reporting). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (the task does NOT instruct an emotion regulation strategy such as cognitive reappraisal, distancing, or acceptance; instead it directs rumination/provocation-focused thought, which is not an instructed regulation strategy). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Because the meta-analysis requires an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (I6), this study must be excluded despite meeting other criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using visual conditioned stimuli (geometric figures) and reports within-task contrasts (e.g., CS+E vs CS-) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates. The task involves passive viewing/conditioned responding rather than instructed emotion-regulation, but the meta-analysis objective explicitly allows studies that view visual emotional stimuli without regulation. The sample is appropriate and analyses include whole-brain corrected results and coordinate reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-only) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI experiment using visual stimuli and reports within-task contrasts and standard coordinate results (satisfying I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11). However, it does NOT meet I6: there was no explicit, experimentally instructed emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., instructed reappraisal, distancing, acceptance). Participants were instructed to look/fixate and religious participants later reported spontaneous detachment/reappraisal-like strategies in post-scan reports, but these were not instructed manipulations during the task. Because I6 is required, the study is excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to reappraise negative visual stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > Negative and Negative > Reappraise) at the group level, with whole-brain voxelwise analyses corrected for multiple comparisons and coordinates reported in tables/figures. Sample (adult, healthy) is acceptable. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references).

This is a task-based fMRI study in which participants were explicitly instructed to regulate emotion (audio prompts to ‘increase’ or ‘decrease’) while viewing visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts ('increase vs attend', 'decrease vs attend') and shows whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction (group-level results and coordinates referenced). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I11. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply: the paper is empirical, includes whole-brain analyses (not only ROI/seed/connectivity), and reports within-task effects rather than only between-group interactions. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly tests instructed cognitive reappraisal of visual emotional stimuli (personally craved food images). The full text reports the experimental methods, participant sample, stimulus materials (visual food images), and a within-subjects design comparing regulate vs look (and choice manipulations). Behavioral and neuroimaging analyses include within-task contrasts (regulate > look, look > regulate) and group-level whole-brain random-effects univariate analyses with cluster correction and reported clusters/coordinates; unthresholded maps are available on NeuroVault. Multivariate (MVPA) and other analyses are also reported, but the presence of whole-brain task activation maps and peak coordinates satisfies whole-brain evidence requirements. Sample is a normative participant group with results reported at group level. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-visual stimuli, non-empirical) are met. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete for screening purposes.

This study is a longitudinal resting-state and structural MRI RCT in CM-MOH patients that does not include any task-based fMRI or instructed emotion-regulation paradigm. It reports seed-based resting-state functional connectivity and vertex-wise cortical thickness changes, not task-evoked activations to visual emotional stimuli. Therefore it does not meet the core inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Full text is complete. The study is a task-based fMRI investigation with explicit instructions to regulate emotion (I5, I6), includes an appropriate sample (I8), reports within-task regulation contrasts (I9), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates (I10, I11). However, it does NOT meet inclusion I7: participants regulated negative emotion elicited by committing errors during a cognitive task (self-generated, performance-related emotion), not by viewing externally presented emotional visual stimuli such as IAPS pictures, photographic faces/scenes, or film clips. The meta-analysis objective specifies regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli; because the regulated stimulus here is performance error rather than an emotional visual stimulus, the study does not match that core criterion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered.

Full text reports a task-based fMRI study in adolescents using an emotion regulation paradigm that included instructed cognitive reappraisal (“decrease”) and passive viewing (“look”) trials. Emotional stimuli were visual (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (look negative > look neutral) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates (e.g., vmPFC peak X=12, Y=48, Z=−22). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, includes whole-brain task activation maps, not only connectivity-only, and not an empathy/perspective-taking-only paradigm). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (downregulation) and includes visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (downregulate negative > attend negative; attend negative > attend neutral) and group-level whole-brain second-level analyses (one-sample t-tests) with t-maps/coordinates provided in supporting information. Sample and analyses meet eligibility (healthy young adult females; ROIs used but whole-brain results are reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-only; within-group effects are reported; not an empathy task). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11.

The regulation task in this study involved self-generated ‘think happy thoughts’ neurofeedback (thermometer) rather than regulation of responses to externally presented visual emotional stimuli. While the paper is a task-based fMRI study (I5), it instructs emotion regulation (I6), reports within-task contrasts (up-regulation vs down-regulation) (I9), and includes group-level whole-brain analyses/localiser maps (I10/I11), it does NOT meet inclusion criterion I7 because the experimental regulation was not of visual emotional stimuli (the visual face localiser was used only to define ROIs). Therefore the study does not match the meta-analysis requirement that regulation be applied to visual emotional stimuli.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed cognitive emotion regulation (distancing) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS). It reports within-task contrasts related to regulation and unregulated viewing, uses group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses with reported peak coordinates (and ROI corrections for a priori regions), and includes an eligible sample (healthy adults). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is a task-based fMRI study using visual (static face) stimuli with a broad lifespan sample and reports unregulated viewing contrasts (surprised>neutral; fearful>neutral), so it meets I5, I7, I8, and I9. However, it does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (I6 not met) and the report is ROI-focused (amygdala ROIs) with no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps or peak coordinates provided; thus it fails I10. Because the paper reports only ROI analyses without accompanying whole-brain results, exclusion criterion E4 applies. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis that requires whole-brain task-evoked maps (or regulation instructions).

This is a task-based fMRI study using an in-scanner film-based emotion reactivity and regulation paradigm (fMRI acquisition, GLM analyses). An explicit emotion regulation instruction (reappraisal: ‘regulate’ negative) was used. Stimuli were visual (30-second film/video clips). The sample spans ages 23–88 (population-derived cohort). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., watch positive > watch neutral; regulate negative > watch negative) and conducted group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (thresholded at P<0.05 FWE) alongside ROI analyses. Reporting of whole-brain results appears in text/figures/tables. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded: This study reports predictive modeling based on pretreatment whole-brain functional connectivity (FC) in a clinical sample and does not involve a task-based emotion-regulation paradigm with instructed regulation of visual emotional stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample: clinical participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation strategy such as reappraisal), I7 (visual emotional stimuli presentation), I9 (within-task regulation or viewing contrasts like reappraise>look or emotion>baseline), I10 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise activation map). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (study reports only connectivity/resting-state or FC analyses without reporting whole-brain task activation maps). Full text appears complete; therefore excluded.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of approach–avoidance responses to emotional faces and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates. However, it does not instruct participants to use an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., cognitive reappraisal, acceptance, distancing) nor does it include a conventional within-task contrast that indexes instructed emotion regulation (e.g., reappraise > look). The key contrasts (affect-incongruent > affect-congruent in the AA task and Task×Condition interactions) index voluntary control of stimulus–response mappings / motor approach–avoidance behavior rather than an explicit instruction to regulate one’s emotional experience. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation) is not met, and criterion I9 (within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrast as defined by the review) is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I10, I11. Exclusion criteria met: none ( []). Full text appears complete.

This full text meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) in which participants were instructed to regulate emotion using reappraisal/distancing and implementation-intention strategies (I6). Emotional stimuli are visual static images from IAPS (I7). Sample is healthy adult participants (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., regulate > attend; attend > regulation) (I9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates and thresholds (I10), and results are presented in text/tables/figures (I11). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation using visual stimuli (faces) and reports unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., faces > baseline). However, all reported group-level statistical tests were conducted using anatomically restricted small-volume correction (amygdala ROI) and ROI-based extractions; the paper does not present a whole-brain, voxelwise group activation map or whole-brain peak coordinates independent of SVC. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports ONLY ROI/SVC results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: faces), I8 (sample: adolescents allowed), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrasts). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation task), I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation map reported). Full text appears complete and includes methods, results, and discussion.

This is a task-based fMRI study in adolescents using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) presented as task-irrelevant distractors during an emotional Go/NoGo task. The paper reports within-task emotional valence contrasts (aversive > neutral) — an unregulated viewing contrast that matches the review’s acceptable contrast types — and performs whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses with reported cluster peaks in MNI space and tables/figures. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11. The study does not instruct participants to regulate their emotions (I6 not met), but unregulated viewing contrasts are allowed per I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI experiment in which participants were explicitly instructed to regulate their emotional responses (up- and down-regulate) to visual negative pictures using real-time fMRI neurofeedback. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (up vs. down, up/down vs. view) and presents group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (with cluster correction and peak coordinates). Sample is healthy adults (female) and stimulus modality is visual (IAPS and related picture sets). Thus all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply (study is empirical, reports whole-brain activation maps, includes within-group task effects, and is not an empathy/perspective-taking-only design). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study in adolescents using visual social-evaluation stimuli and reports within-task contrasts (Negative>Neutral, Positive>Neutral) and whole-brain analyses (so I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11 are satisfied). However, the study does NOT instruct participants to use any emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other instructed regulation); participants passively received social feedback and rated their affect. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation task). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I6 is not met, the study must be excluded.

The study is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI investigation of responses to emotional words and reports unregulated viewing contrasts (NEG–NEU) with peak coordinates. However, it does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal or other instructed regulation), and the emotional stimuli are words (word/sentence stimuli are explicitly excluded by the review criteria). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 (instructed emotion regulation) and I7 (visual non-word stimuli). No explicit exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrast), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates), I11 (reports acceptable coordinate/figure evidence). Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal to up- and down-regulate responses to negative visual images (IAPS), meeting the review's emotion regulation instruction criterion. The paper reports within-task contrasts (enhance > suppress) related to regulation and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and cluster correction (Tables and figures described), satisfying requirements for reporting and whole-brain evidence. The sample and stimuli meet inclusion criteria. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary material is referenced but not required. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group effects, not an empathy/perspective-taking-only task).

This fMRI study is excluded because the emotional stimuli were auditory (audiotaped stories) rather than visual, thus failing inclusion criterion I7 (visual stimuli required).
