The study does meet multiple inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed regulation strategy: distraction vs engagement), I8 (sample reporting with control group), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported, e.g., anger-distraction vs anger-engagement), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), and I11 (whole-brain results described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore exclusion is based on failing required inclusion criterion I7 (non-visual stimuli). Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is a resting-state fMRI connectivity analysis (seed-based rsFC) relating trait alexithymia to craving in smokers; it does not employ any task-based fMRI or instruct participants to regulate emotional responses to visual stimuli. It therefore fails multiple inclusion criteria for this review. Exclusion rationale: E5 applies (reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without any whole-brain task activation maps). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample of participants of any age/group is reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not task-based fMRI), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli/tasks), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or viewing contrasts reported), I10/I11 (no task-evoked whole-brain, voxelwise activation maps reported). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study (emotion-word Stroop) reporting whole-brain contrasts (unpleasant>neutral, pleasant>neutral) with coordinates, and an eligible sample. However, it does NOT meet core eligibility for the review: (a) there was no instructed emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal/suppression/distancing instruction) — inclusion I6 not met; (b) the emotional stimuli were words (emotion-word Stroop), and the review excludes studies that use word/sentence stimuli rather than visual images/clips — inclusion I7 not met. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E7) were triggered. Therefore the study is excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to regulate emotional responses (down-regulation) during presentation of visual aversive pictures. The sample (healthy adult females) is eligible. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., REGULATE>VIEW, VIEW>REGULATE) and performs group-level, whole-brain random effects analyses with reported activation clusters and peak coordinates (e.g., right amygdala peak [24, -7, -14]), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided content appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11) and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive distraction (0-back vs 2-back) during anticipation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures). The study reports within-task contrasts examining the effect of cognitive load on anticipatory emotional processing (including interaction contrasts showing reduced amygdala and MPFC activation during high-load distraction), and group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment that uses visual threat cues and reports within-task contrasts, but it does not instruct participants to use an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal) — instead it manipulates social contact (handholding). Importantly, the analysis is ROI-based using an independent threat map rather than reporting a group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation map with peak coordinates from the present sample. Thus it fails the emotion-regulation instruction criterion and the whole-brain reporting requirement.

Exclusion: E7 applies — this is an empathy/perspective-taking fMRI study (intentional empathy) with no instruction to amplify or dampen emotional responses (no instructed emotion regulation such as reappraisal, distancing, acceptance). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli — face photographs), I8 (acceptable sample), I9 (reports within-task contrasts including unregulated viewing contrasts like ‘intentional empathy for familiar angry > baseline’), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported activations), I11 (coordinates and whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy). Because I6 is required and E7 explicitly excludes empathy/perspective-taking without regulation instruction, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal as an emotion-regulation strategy (NegReapp) while participants view visual IAPS images. It includes both a clinical (FND) group and age/sex-matched healthy controls with group results reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., NegReapp vs. NegW, NegW vs. NegDistr) and presents group-level, voxelwise results with MNI peak coordinates and FWE correction; ROI/SVC analyses are reported but whole-brain analyses and coordinates are also provided (satisfying whole-brain evidence and reporting standards). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so the available content is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (increase/decrease) while participants view visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (increase > attend; decrease < attend), conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and Talairach peak coordinates, and also reports ROI analyses. The sample (older adults) is eligible per review criteria. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and not an empathy task without regulation). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli and reports within-task contrasts; however, participants were not instructed to use an explicit emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, up-/down-regulation). The task probes implicit/automatic attentional control (attend-to-face vs. attend-to-scene and categorize threat vs. neutral) rather than instructed regulation. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (instruction of an emotion-regulation strategy) is not met. Other inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed an emotion-regulation strategy (expressive suppression via ‘Control’ cues) using visual stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (NS vs NL), provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM results with MNI coordinates and figures, and reports separate participant groups (StD and HC). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies I5–I11 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

Exclusion E4: The study’s task-based fMRI results are reported via ROI analyses (hippocampus and intraparietal sulcus) rather than a group-level, whole-brain task activation map with peak coordinates. Met inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI with NF runs), I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy — recall of positive autobiographical memories), I7 (visual emotional stimuli used in view blocks — IAPS pictures), I8 (healthy adult sample reported), I9 (within-task contrasts reported, e.g., regulate > baseline, view > baseline, regulate > view). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-evoked statistical map with peak coordinates is reported). Because I10 is required and E4 applies, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Although this is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports group-level whole-brain activation maps with coordinates, it does not meet the review’s requirement that participants regulate an emotional response to externally presented visual stimuli. The task instructs participants to generate/up-regulate internal emotional states (tenderness, anguish) using personalized cognitive strategies and music and uses a virtual environment only as feedback. Thus the emotional stimuli are not external visual stimuli being regulated, and the paradigm is an emotion induction/neurofeedback task rather than instructed regulation (e.g., reappraisal) of a presented visual stimulus. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (film clips; I7). The paper reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (Sad > Neutral) relevant to emotion processing (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, reported with standard-space coordinates and cluster inference (I10,I11). The sample and reporting are appropriate (I8). Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction was used (i.e., this is not a reappraisal task), the meta-analysis accepts unregulated viewing contrasts; therefore the study fits the review objective. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: photographs of peers/faces), I8 (sample: adolescents; clinical group reported separately), I9 (within-task contrasts: negative > positive feedback/unregulated viewing contrast), I10 (group-level whole-brain results reported with peak coordinates), I11 (coordinates and results described in text/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 — the study did not instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other instructed regulation); participants simply received/observed peer feedback and were not told to regulate their emotional responses. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to satisfy I6 (instruction of an emotion regulation strategy) despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

Exclusion reason: E4 (reporting only region-limited/partial-brain results). Inclusion met: I7 (visual stimuli: computer task), I8 (sample: children), I9 (within-task contrast: frustration > baseline). Inclusion NOT met: I5 (not task-based fMRI — study used fNIRS), I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; participants were not instructed to reappraise or otherwise regulate), I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level fMRI maps with standard-space peak coordinates), I11 (not applicable — no whole-brain results reported). Full text appears complete and methods/results/discussion are present. Therefore excluded because the study modality and analysis do not meet core fMRI/whole-brain requirements (E4).

This is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs antecedent-focused cognitive emotion regulation (attend vs regulate) during presentation of visual stimuli (colored squares predicting monetary reward). It reports within-task contrasts (CS+ vs CS−; regulate vs attend) and group-level activation results with regions and supplementary tables (striatal and prefrontal activations), indicating whole-brain analyses. Sample and methods are reported in full text. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study reports a simultaneous task-based EEG-fMRI experiment in which participants were instructed to ‘watch’ or ‘decrease’ (cognitive reappraisal) while viewing visual emotional images (IAPS). fMRI data were acquired during the task, preprocessed in SPM8 with normalization to MNI space, and an EEG-informed GLM was used to identify task-relevant, group-level whole-brain activations that were used as fMRI priors. The paper contrasts negative-reappraisal vs negative-watch and reports activation differences across cortical regions; networks were constructed from these whole-brain source estimates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. These features satisfy inclusion criteria I5–I11. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met.

While this is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli and whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11), it does NOT instruct an emotion regulation strategy. The Emotional Conflict (emotional Stroop) task required labeling emotions/ignoring words but did not instruct participants to up-/down-regulate or reappraise their emotional responses; therefore inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion rationale: This study used resting-state fMRI and spectral DCM (effective connectivity) combined with ecological momentary assessment; it does not include any task-based emotion-regulation paradigm or within-task contrasts, nor does it present whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports ONLY resting-state/effective connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample includes clinical and control groups; controls are reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation task/cognitive reappraisal), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli presented; resting-state), I9 (no within-task regulation or viewing contrasts reported), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked maps). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion provided). Hence the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis focused on task-based emotion regulation fMRI.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study with visual stimuli (video clips) and an adequate sample, and it reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses (MNI coordinates) and within-task regressions of emotion-related contrasts, it does NOT include an instructed emotion-regulation task. Participants were told to ‘think back to the anagram task’ and let thoughts come naturally while viewing videos; no reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other instructed regulation strategy was given. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation strategy) is not met. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that used visual emotional stimuli (IAPS and photographs) and reports unregulated viewing contrasts (negative > neutral) during picture viewing. The sample is healthy adult participants and meets sample inclusion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected clusters) and describes significant clusters and peaks, satisfying whole-brain evidence and reporting standards. There is no indication of exclusion criteria being met (e.g., only ROI or connectivity results). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis of studies that view or regulate visual emotional stimuli.

This study does not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses; it uses a passive art-viewing paradigm with monetary sponsorship manipulation and measures valuation/preference. Inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy) is not met. The study does meet other inclusion criteria (task-based fMRI; visual stimuli; eligible sample; reports within-task contrasts of passive viewing/value encoding; appears to include whole-brain voxelwise analyses and adequate reporting), but because it lacks an instructed regulation condition it does not address the review objective of studies that instruct emotion regulation vs. view-only contrasts. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs attentional deployment (an emotion-regulation strategy) while participants view visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts directly relevant to regulation (e.g., unpleasant non-arousing focus > unpleasant arousing focus and related comparisons), includes healthy adult participants, and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak activations (tables/supplementary coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and supplemental coordinate lists are referenced. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal/downregulation during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The sample (pregnant and naturally cycling controls) is eligible. The paper reports within-task contrasts (downregulation > view) and provides group-level whole-brain results with MNI coordinates (e.g., left MFG -41,7,49), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using an affect-labeling task (explicit labeling of visual facial stimuli) which functions as an emotion-regulation-related instruction. Stimuli are visual (photographs of faces). The paper reports within-task contrasts (affect labeling vs fixation/gender; pre-post and group contrasts), provides group-level voxelwise results with MNI coordinates, and includes whole-brain/exploratory analyses. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed cognitive reappraisal in children (6–10 yrs) using visual stimuli (IAPS/EmoPicS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation (negative-decrease vs. negative-attend; negative-attend vs. neutral-attend) and describes group-level voxelwise/random-effects whole-brain analyses with results reported in MNI space (peak coordinates/tables and supplemental voxelwise results). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (faces) and reports unregulated viewing contrasts (emotional face-matching: emotion > shape) with whole-brain group-level analyses (FWE cluster-corrected) and reported coordinates for brain-behavior correlations. The methods, results, and discussion are fully present. Thus it meets criteria for task-based fMRI (I5), visual stimuli (I7), reporting an unregulated viewing contrast relevant to emotion processing (I9), providing whole-brain evidence with coordinates/voxelwise maps (I10), and acceptable reporting in text/figures/supplementary materials (I11). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional images during an N-back task (I5, I7). The sample and reported within-task contrasts (e.g., combat vs neutral; cognitive load effects) meet I8 and I9. However, the study reports ROI-based analyses only and explicitly states BOLD detection was limited to specific ROIs; no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps or peak coordinates in standard space are reported. Thus it fails I10 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI results/no whole-brain analysis). Additionally, no explicit instructed emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal) was used (I6 not met), though unregulated viewing contrasts are present. Because E4 is met, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion-regulation paradigm (Look vs Decrease; cognitive reappraisal), with visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Negative Decrease vs Negative Look; Neutral Decrease vs Neutral Look), includes both bipolar patients and healthy controls with separate analyses, and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (voxel thresholding and cluster-based correction) with results reported in main and supplementary materials. The full text contains background, methods, results and discussion, so is complete for screening. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This is a task-based fMRI protocol/empirical study of bereaved older adults that uses visual emotional stimuli (faces) and reports unregulated viewing contrasts (fear+anger > shapes) and whole-brain activation maps. However, none of the tasks involve an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance); participants performed face–shape matching and a Stop-Signal Task, not regulation instructions. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (instructed emotion regulation) is not met. I also did not find explicit reporting of peak coordinates for task activation maps in standard space (potentially affecting I10), though whole-brain maps are shown. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrast). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed regulation), I10 (no explicit peak coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) appear to be triggered. Given failure to meet all required inclusion criteria (notably I6), the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (dynamic faces) and reports within-task emotion>control contrasts (implicit/unregulated viewing). Group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses were conducted (cluster-level correction using AlphaSim) and regional coordinates are reported, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Although the study also reports effective connectivity (DCM), it additionally provides task activation results rather than only connectivity analyses. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion for unregulated viewing contrasts of visual emotional stimuli and is eligible for the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation strategies (ACCEPT and SUPPRESS) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (fearful film clips), with both BPD and healthy control groups reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts (acceptance > passive viewing; suppression > passive viewing) and conducts whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (cluster-level thresholding, ROI and whole-brain results reported). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because exclusion criteria E4 and E6 are met: (E4) the imaging analyses were conducted within an a priori frontolimbic/striatal ROI mask (region-of-interest restricted voxelwise results) with no accompanying whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis reported; (E6) the paper reports primarily between-group (CET vs TAU) posttreatment contrasts and does not present group-level within-task activation maps for any group. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed effortful emotion-regulation paradigm — attend to working memory and inhibit responses to emotional face distractors), I7 (visual stimuli: static face images), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task contrasts of emotional vs neutral faces were used as contrasts). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain group-level, voxelwise task activation map reported). Full text appears complete.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal) using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). It reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > view), includes both a clinical (MDD) and healthy control group with results reported separately, and presents group-level whole-brain analyses (voxelwise statistics with correction and reported activation peaks). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I11) and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive emotion regulation (detachment/reappraisal) vs permit, using visual stimuli (IAPS/EmoPicS) in healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Negative Permit > Negative Detach and reverse) and presents group-level, whole-brain second-level analyses with peak coordinates and thresholding (FWE), meeting criteria for whole-brain evidence. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, connectivity-only analyses, non-empirical paper, or empathy-without-regulation) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that tests instructed (implicit) emotion regulation via attentional deployment (attend-to-face vs. attend-to-word) in participants with PTSD and healthy controls. Stimuli are visual (faces with embedded trauma or neutral words), participants are explicitly instructed to shift attention (an instructed cognitive control/implicit regulation strategy), and the study reports within-task effects relating brain-state regulation and encoding of feedback. Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses were conducted (data normalized to an MNI template; cluster-wise results reported across regions such as insula, MFG, hippocampus and pgACC), and results are described in the text and figures. The sample includes a clinical PTSD group and a control group with separate analyses. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and therefore appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy/perspective-taking only) apply based on the provided content.

Exclusion E5 met: the study reports only ICA-based network analyses (component spatial maps and component time-course GLMs) and group-level comparisons at the network/component level, but does not present a conventional whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation contrast with peak coordinates in standard space. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: cognitive reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli: negative and neutral pictures), I8 (sample includes clinical groups and healthy controls reported separately), and I9 (within-task contrasts of interest: Maintain > Observe and Regulate > Maintain, albeit at component-level). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map with peak coordinates reported). Therefore the study must be excluded under E5.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to down-regulate negative emotion via cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise vs Maintain). Visual stimuli (IAPS pictures) were used. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation via psychophysiological interaction (Reappraise > Maintain) and provides group-level, voxelwise results with peak coordinates (Table 1, figures). A conjunction whole-brain analysis (Maintain > Baseline AND Reappraise > Baseline) identifying a left amygdala cluster is also reported. The sample (healthy adults) is eligible and behavioral ratings confirm regulation success. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI-only results or only connectivity without whole-brain maps) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual fearful-face stimuli in clinical and control groups, but the paper reports only ROI-based effective connectivity (dynamic effective connectivity/Granger causality) and ROI eigenvariate activation analyses rather than any group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps or peak coordinates. The meta-analysis requires at least one whole-brain task activation analysis (I10) or within-task regulation/viewing contrast (I9). Although participants were instructed to self-label their fear (intended to engage top-down modulation), there is no standard instructed regulation contrast (e.g., reappraise>look) and no whole-brain activation tables/coordinates. Thus it meets I5, I7, I8 but does not meet I9 or I10, and it violates exclusion criteria E5 and E4 (reports only effective/connectivity and ROI-limited results with no whole-brain task maps). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and selective attention) while viewing visual (film) stimuli, with within-task contrasts reported and peak coordinates provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I11. However, all reported voxelwise analyses were conducted within an explicit amygdala–PFC mask (ROI/masked analyses) rather than as a whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis. The paper therefore reports only region-of-interest/partial-brain results with no accompanying whole-brain task activation map, which meets exclusion criterion E4. Because E4 is met (no whole-brain analysis), the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

The article is a task-based fMRI pharmacological study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (distancing) vs look conditions using visual IAPS images (social negative and neutral). It reports within-task contrasts and behavioral reappraisal success (LookNeg − DisNeg) and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (full-factorial ANOVAs) with peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction (e.g., posterior insula coordinates reported) as well as SVC for the amygdala. Sample is healthy adult males (N=65). Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the review (task-based fMRI; instructed emotion regulation; visual stimuli; acceptable sample; within-task contrasts reported; whole-brain group-level maps with coordinates; reporting in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (ROIs-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-only tasks) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria and reports only ROI-based results. Exclusion IDs met: E4 (reports only ROI/small-volume results with no whole-brain, voxelwise task activation map). Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI study) and I8 (adolescent sample). Inclusion IDs NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as cognitive reappraisal; regulation was performed by the mother via dyadic neurofeedback rather than participant-instructed regulation), I7 (regulated stimuli were autobiographical verbal descriptions, not visual stimuli/images or videos), I9 (no standard within-task regulation contrast like “reappraise>look” or equivalent participant-instructed regulation contrast), I10 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it does NOT meet inclusion criterion I7: the regulated emotional stimuli are not visual. The provocation paradigm uses social/interactive cues and auditory white-noise punishments rather than emotional visual stimuli (e.g., IAPS images, faces, or film clips), so it does not address the review objective of regulation of visual emotional stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instruction to use cognitive reappraisal), I8 (eligible participant sample), I9 (reports within-task contrasts such as win>lose and lose>win), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), and I11 (whole-brain results described/tabled). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (visual stimuli). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) were triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the core emotion-regulation instruction requirement (I6) and appears to report only region-focused BOLD results rather than a whole-brain voxelwise task map (violating I10 / matching exclusion E4). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—faces), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports task-related BOLD contrast for threat vs neutral). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; the task is a go/no-go requiring response inhibition but not explicit reappraisal or instructed regulation), I10 (no evidence of a group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation map with peak coordinates in standard space; analyses focus on frontolimbic ROIs). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (results are reported for specific regions/frontolimbic ROIs with no clear whole-brain analysis reported). Full text appears complete for screening (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Given these gaps relative to the meta-analysis objective, exclude this study.

This is a task-based event-related fMRI study that explicitly instructs emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal, suppression, view) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS and in-house pictures). It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., view>reappraise, reappraise>suppress), whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and cluster thresholds, and supplementary ROI connectivity analyses. Participants are healthy adults, and the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal) and also includes affect labeling, using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Reappraise > Observe, Label > Observe) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates in standard MNI space (tables/figures). Participant sample (healthy older adults) is acceptable. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a single-arm clinical trial of an Amyg-EFP neurofeedback intervention in PTSD patients, not a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation to visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample includes clinical participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no task-based fMRI paradigm reported), I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation task such as reappraisal; regulation was implicit during neurofeedback rather than an instructed reappraisal of visual stimuli), I7 (no report of visual emotional stimuli presentation during an fMRI task), I9 (no within-task contrasts like 'reappraise > look' reported), I10 (no whole-brain group-level task activation maps/coordinates reported), I11 (not applicable because above were not satisfied). No exclusion criteria from E3–E7 apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study does not meet the review’s fMRI task-based inclusion requirements and is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures) in a Hariri picture-matching task and reports within-task contrasts of negative vs. neutral (an unregulated viewing contrast). Whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses are reported with peak coordinates and cluster-level inference. Sample characteristics meet eligibility. The study did not instruct an explicit emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met), but the review objective and inclusion criterion I9 allow unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., negative > neutral), so the study qualifies for inclusion as an unregulated viewing task. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets several inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5); it instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal; Regulate vs Attend) (I6); the stimuli are visual (CS squares and cigarette images) (I7); the sample (adult smokers) is an eligible participant group (I8); and the paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Attend CS+ vs Regulate CS+) (I9). However, the full text provided does not report peak coordinates for whole-brain group-level voxelwise statistical maps in a standard anatomical space (MNI or Talairach) that would satisfy I10. Although a group-level whole-brain analysis was performed and ROIs were examined, I10 explicitly requires peak coordinates for whole-brain results; these coordinates are not present in the supplied full text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered by the available content. Because I10 is not met, the study cannot be included for coordinate-based meta-analysis.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation that instructs participants to regulate emotional responses (forgiveness vs. unforgiveness using reappraisal and perspective-taking strategies), includes a suitable sample, and reports within-task whole-brain contrasts and results. However, the emotional stimuli are script-driven narrative scenarios presented as written text to elicit mental imagery rather than visual emotional stimuli (static images, photos, or film clips). This fails inclusion criterion I7 (stimuli must be VISUAL). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded solely because it does not meet I7.

The article reports an empirical, task-based fMRI study of explicit emotion regulation using instructed strategies (reappraisal and response modulation) while participants viewed visual stimuli (IAPS images). Sample: healthy adult participants (n=24). Analyses include within-task contrasts (regulate vs maintain; increase vs decrease) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates reported in MNI space. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are satisfied and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) with a clinical sample reported separately (I8) and includes whole-brain group-level task contrasts (I10). However, it does NOT meet the review's key content requirements: the task examines directed forgetting of words (memory control) rather than an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (violates I6), and the stimuli are written words rather than visual images/films (violates I7). The reported within-task contrasts (F-NG > R-NG) index memory-control/forgetting, not an emotion-regulation contrast of visual stimuli (I9 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore exclude for failure to meet I6, I7, and I9 despite meeting I5, I8, and I10.

This is a task-based fMRI study that includes an instructed emotion regulation task (ER: suppress vs feel), using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The methods describe within-task condition modeling and contrasts (Suppress/Feel/Baseline) and report task-related voxelwise statistical maps (ICA-derived whole-brain component maps with voxelwise thresholds, cluster correction, and reported peaks/cluster statistics). Participants are healthy adults and meet sample eligibility. The paper provides group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (ICA components and GLM second-level results) presented in figures and described in text. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I5–I11). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to regulate emotional responses (imitation to up-regulate and expressive suppression to down-regulate) while viewing dynamic visual facial stimuli. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported with contrasts directly testing regulation (IMT>eSUP, eSUP>IMT, IMT>GND) and coordinate-based results/figures are provided. The sample is healthy volunteers and the full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use a cognitive reappraisal (mentalizing-reappraisal) strategy during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS pictures in training and photographs of proposers/offers during the Dictator Game). The sample is healthy adults. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., UP > LOOK, DOWN > LOOK, DOWN < LOOK < UP), whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with correction and coordinate tables/figures, and also describes ROI and DCM analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal: upregulate and downregulate) using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to the review (upregulate > permit, downregulate > permit, permit-negative > permit-neutral) and presents whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses with cluster-level correction and peak coordinates in MNI space. Both patient groups and healthy controls are reported separately. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, and is not an empathy-only perspective task). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I11 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli and whole-brain/group-level voxelwise analyses (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11). However, participants were not given any explicit instruction to regulate their emotions (no cognitive reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other instructed regulation); instead the authors manipulated pay context to implicitly alter emotion-related processing. Therefore the study does NOT meet inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion regulation strategy). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. Exclusion criteria met: none (E: []). Because I6 is required and not met, the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (regulate vs look) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS photographs). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to review (regulate negative > look negative; look negative > look neutral) and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak MNI coordinates and figures. Sample characteristics (community adult sample) are reported and analyses include whole-brain results as well as ROI checks. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I5–I11) and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using visual IAPS pictures and explicit instruction to ‘permit’ (accept) versus ‘view’ negative stimuli, i.e., an instructed emotion-regulation baseline comparison. The paper reports within-task contrasts (permit negative > view negative; view negative > view neutral) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected peak results alongside ROI analyses. The sample and methods are clearly described and the full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the review are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study with an appropriate sample and reports within-task emotion contrasts (e.g. negative olfactory > neutral), but it does NOT meet two core inclusion criteria: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy — the manipulation is implicit/passive music-listening, participants were not instructed to regulate) and I7 (stimuli are non-visual — auditory and olfactory stimuli only). Therefore it is ineligible for a meta-analysis restricted to instructed regulation of VISUAL emotional stimuli. No exclusion criteria from the list are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed cognitive emotion regulation (reappraisal: downregulate/upregulate/maintain) using visual IAPS images, tested within-subject contrasts (e.g. downregulate > maintain, negative > neutral), and reports group-level whole-brain activation results (maps/coordinates and Neurovault links). Participants include younger and older adults and within-task contrasts and whole-brain analyses are present. Full-text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for task fMRI reappraisal studies and does not trigger exclusion criteria (whole-brain analyses are reported despite some partial-coverage exclusions).

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation using cognitive reappraisal (Re-Interpret) on visual stimuli (distressing and smoking pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts directly relevant to emotion regulation (ReappraiseDistressing > LookDistressing and ReappraiseSmoking > LookSmoking) and describes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (inclusive 3-way conjunction and reported clusters; supplementary tables with coordinates are referenced). The sample (treatment-seeking smokers) is an eligible participant group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal to down-regulate emotion while viewing visual stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing reappraisal and control (e.g., RU–CU, (CU–CN)–(RU–RN)), and presents group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates (MNI converted to Talairach) and thresholding. Sample and methods are fully described. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

Exclusion due to E4: the paper reports ROI-based second-level analyses (paired t-tests in predefined anatomical ROIs) with no indication of group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or peak coordinates in standard space. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion-regulation strategy—acceptance), I8 (clinical sample of anorexia nervosa patients), and I9 (within-task regulation contrast: ACCEPT > SAU). Inclusion criteria not met: I10 (no evidence of whole-brain group-level voxelwise activation maps or reported coordinates). I7 (visual nature of stimuli) is unclear from the full text and therefore not confidently met. Full text appears complete for core content. Given the ROI-only reporting and lack of whole-brain results, the study must be excluded per E4.

This is a task-based event-related fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (colored faces) with explicit within-task contrasts comparing emotional versus neutral faces (e.g., angry > neutral). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates (FDR-corrected results converted to Talairach space) and presents coordinate tables and detailed text descriptions. Although no emotion-regulation instruction (I6) was given, the review objective accepts unregulated viewing contrasts; the study therefore satisfies the alternative inclusion criterion (I9). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and is complete for screening purposes.

Exclusion due to lack of required whole-brain, voxelwise task-activation results. (a) Exclusion IDs met: E4, E5 — the study reports task-based dynamic functional connectivity and graph/parcel-based network metrics (Schaefer 300-node parcellation) rather than group-level, voxelwise task activation maps with reported peak coordinates; analyses are connectivity/parcellation-based rather than whole-brain voxelwise activation. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (explicit instructed emotion regulation — cognitive reappraisal task), I7 (visual stimuli — IAPS images), I8 (sample criteria met). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I9 (no clear reporting of within-task voxelwise contrasts such as “reappraise > look” with peak coordinates), I10 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps with peak coordinates), I11 (no voxelwise coordinate tables/figures described). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an affect-labeling task (implicit emotion regulation) with instructed regulation (label vs match). Stimuli were visual (facial expressions). Sample includes adolescents. The paper reports within-task contrasts isolating regulation (negative label > negative match; positive label > positive match) and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME1) with peak coordinates reported (e.g., bilateral mPFC). Thus all inclusion criteria are met, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the core inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none of the explicit exclusion criteria E3–E7 apply. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I8 (sample: adolescent participants qualify). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study — uses fNIRS), I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; task is a psychosocial stress task, not reappraisal/acceptance/etc.), I7 (stimuli are not visual emotional stimuli — TSST interpersonal stress, not visual images/videos), I9 (does not report within-task emotion-regulation contrasts such as reappraise>look or similar), I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise fMRI maps/standard-space peak coordinates reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper is ineligible for inclusion in this fMRI emotion-regulation meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli and within-task contrasts, but it does not instruct participants to use an emotion-regulation strategy. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: horror film clips/videos), I8 (sample includes clinical participants), I9 (reports within-task/unregulated viewing contrasts and task-based activations), I10 (group-level whole-brain task analyses reported), I11 (reporting consistent with acceptable whole-brain results). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal, acceptance, distancing, or instructed cognitive control). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered (e.g., ROI-only or connectivity-only reporting). Therefore the study must be excluded because it does not satisfy the required emotion-regulation instruction criterion (I6). Full text appears complete.

This is an empathy/perspective-taking fMRI study using a task that asks participants to rate others’ emotions (empathic accuracy), not to deliberately regulate their own emotional responses. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: video clips), I8 (sample includes adolescents). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal, distancing, acceptance—participants were instructed to evaluate others’ emotions, not to amplify/dampen their own), I9 (no within-task contrasts of instructed regulation vs. view/maintain; analyses relate empathic accuracy to activation rather than contrasts like “reappraise > look”), I10 (while voxel-wise analyses are reported, the paper does not provide a clear within-task whole-brain regulation contrast with peak coordinates for a regulation contrast). Exclusion criteria met: E7 (empathy/perspective-taking study with no instruction to regulate own emotion). Therefore the study does not address the review’s required paradigm of instructed emotion regulation and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and suppression) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (video clips). The sample (healthy adults) is eligible. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., reappraise > watch, suppression > watch), performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and provides peak coordinates in standard anatomical space. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or absence of within-task effects) are met.

This is a task-based fMRI randomized controlled trial that directly instructs emotion regulation (regulate vs. attend) using an Emotion Regulation Task, with contrasts reported for negative downregulation > negative attend and positive upregulation > positive attend. Stimuli were visual emotional pictures, participants were adults remitted from recurrent MDD (clinical sample reported separately), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with MNI peak coordinates, cluster sizes, and corrected statistics. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective and should be included.

Exclusion E4: the study reports only ROI-focused analyses (a priori ROI spheres and percent signal-change extractions) rather than a reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation map with peak coordinates. Inclusion met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: negative pictures), I8 (sample qualifies: healthy college participants), I9 (within-task contrasts related to regulation: inhibition vs neutral and implicit vs explicit reported). Inclusion NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy — the study relies on implicit priming rather than instructions to reappraise/distancing/accept), I10 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise results/peak coordinates reported). Full text appears complete.

This study is a resting-state 7T fMRI investigation with fALFF and seed-based connectivity analyses; it contains no task, no instructed emotion-regulation paradigm, and no task-evoked within-task contrasts. Exclusion criterion met: E5 (reports only resting-state and connectivity analyses without any whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criterion met: I8 (sample of clinical and control groups qualifies). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not task-based fMRI), I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli presented), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts reported), I10 (no task-evoked whole-brain task activation maps). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper does not address the review objective and should be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs an emotion regulation strategy (distancing/reappraisal) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS images). The study reports within-task contrasts comparing 'negative regulate' versus 'negative permit' and complementary 'negative permit' versus 'neutral permit'. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and peak coordinates in MNI space are reported for amygdala and PFC results. A clinical sample (MS with and without depression) is included and group comparisons are reported separately. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (task, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, statistics), Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, reports within-task effects, not an empathy/perspective-taking task without regulation). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based, event-related fMRI study using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures) with healthy adult samples (young and older), and it reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (negative > neutral) and associated behavioral correlations. The paper includes whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with coordinate-based results and tables/figures, satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Although the reported results focus on the spontaneous (unregulated) run, the meta-analysis objective explicitly includes studies that view stimuli without regulating; therefore the study qualifies. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only reports, non-empirical) are met. Full text is complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria applied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (whole-brain group-level maps/coordinates), I11 (results clearly described in text/tables). Exclusion criteria applied: [].

This study used task-based fMRI with visual stimuli (violent vs. non-violent video game) in a healthy sample and reports voxelwise peak coordinates for results; however, it did not instruct participants to perform an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal/distancing/other instructed regulation). Importantly, the reported results are seed-based task-related functional connectivity (amygdala connectivity) contrasts rather than whole-brain task-evoked activation maps; the paper does not present group-level whole-brain activation (univariate) contrasts for viewing vs. baseline. Per exclusion criterion E5 (studies reporting ONLY seed-based/effective connectivity without also reporting a whole-brain task activation map), this study must be excluded. Met inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies), I11 (coordinates/cluster reporting). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation), I9 (no within-task univariate activation contrast relevant to regulation/viewing reported), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map reported).

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual stimuli (videos of faces; I7). The paradigm includes an unregulated viewing contrast (Approach > Static), satisfying the requirement for within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (I9). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses are reported with peak coordinates (e.g., hippocampus 28 −16 −10), meeting whole-brain evidence and reporting requirements (I10, I11). The sample includes patients and matched healthy controls with results reported separately (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-without-regulation design). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Although no explicit instructed emotion-regulation strategy was used (I6 not applicable), the meta-analysis objective accepts studies that involve viewing without regulation; thus this study is eligible. Therefore I include the study.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal of drug cues and savoring of food cues) using visual stimuli (static images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise drug > look drug; look drug > look neutral/food) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FSL FLAME mixed-effects, cluster thresholds) with results described and referenced to supplements/tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I11 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-only design).

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual IAPS images with an implicit reappraisal manipulation (spoken neutral vs negative sentences preceding images) that functions as an emotion-regulation cue. The authors report within-task contrasts (NeutNeg vs NeutNeut) related to regulation and provide whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses with MNI peak coordinates and TFCE-corrected maps. Sample (SSD patients) is acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and task effects are reported). Full text is complete.

Exclusion (E4) applies: the fMRI acquisition for the neurofeedback runs used limited field-of-view (15 slices covering mOFC, temporal lobe and parts of visual cortex), and the authors explicitly note restricted brain coverage as a limitation; no true whole-brain group-level voxelwise activation map with whole-brain coverage is reported, so the study lacks the required whole-brain task-evoked analysis (I10 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation task — up/downregulation of amygdala), I7 (visual emotional face stimuli), I8 (eligible sample: healthy adults), I9 (within-task contrasts: regulation > baseline and related analyses), I11 (results and maps/coordinates reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (whole-brain evidence). Therefore exclude under E4. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is a structural MRI and resting-state functional connectivity investigation of neighborhood socioeconomic disadvantage in traumatically injured adults. It does not include any task-based fMRI or instructed emotion-regulation paradigm, nor does it report within-task regulation contrasts or whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Therefore it does not meet the review’s task-based emotion regulation requirements.

This is a resting-state fMRI study with no task-based emotion-regulation paradigm. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only resting-state/functional connectivity analyses without any whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample: adolescents). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli presented during a task), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), I11 (no task-based whole-brain results reported in text/tables). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion relevant to resting-state analyses, but it does not address the meta-analysis objective requiring task-evoked emotion regulation or viewing contrasts. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual stimuli (IAPS images) and reports group-level whole-brain univariate and multivariate results; it meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11. However, participants were instructed to rate/view images and there was no instructed emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing) nor any within-task regulation contrast (e.g., reappraise > look). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (no instructed emotion regulation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the regulated stimuli are non-visual: the task (MIST) uses mental arithmetic with time pressure and performance feedback to induce psychosocial stress rather than presenting visual emotional stimuli (pictures or video). Therefore inclusion criterion I7 (visual emotional stimuli) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed cognitive regulation of emotional/stress response), I8 (sample includes patient and control groups), I9 (within-task regulation vs non-regulation effects reported), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I11 (whole-brain results described). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation (reappraise/savor) using visual stimuli (IAPS), with appropriate participant sample and within-task contrasts and group-level voxelwise analyses reported. Therefore it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation—reappraisal/savoring), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies), and I9 (reports within-task contrasts related to regulation). However, the provided full text does not include peak coordinates (in MNI/Talairach) for group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps nor any tables/figures/supplementary coordinates in the excerpt provided, so I cannot verify I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps with peak coordinates in standard space) or I11 (that such coordinates/results are reported in tables/figures/supplement). Because I10 is a required inclusion criterion and cannot be confirmed from the provided text, the study is excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met.

This fMRI study used task-based scanning of a visual (film) stimulus and reports within-task comparisons of high vs. low anger epochs, but it does not meet key inclusion requirements for the review. Specifically, the task did NOT instruct participants to apply an emotion regulation strategy (I6 not met); instead participants passively viewed the movie and any regulation was implicit. Critically, the paper does not report a group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map with peak coordinates in standard space (I10 not met). Rather, analyses are ROI-based dependency/network (D NA) and connectivity-focused. Therefore this study violates exclusion criteria E4 (reports only ROI-based results/no whole-brain analysis) and E5 (reports only connectivity/effective-connectivity analyses without accompanying whole-brain task activation maps). Although inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: film), I8 (sample acceptable), and I9 (within-task contrast: high vs low anger epochs) are satisfied, failure to meet I6 and I10 and presence of E4 and E5 lead to exclusion.

The study is EXCLUDED because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: participants were not instructed to use an emotion regulation strategy. Although the task is a task-based fMRI study (I5), uses visual emotional stimuli (faces) (I7), includes an eligible sample (I8), reports within-task contrasts related to emotional processing (informative vs. confirmatory; high vs. low intensity) (I9), and provides whole-brain group-level analyses with reported coordinates (I10, I11), it investigates implicit/automatic regulation via feedback anticipation rather than an instructed regulation strategy (no reappraisal/distancing/acceptance instruction). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion-regulation strategies (acceptance and intensification) during presentation of visual symptom-triggering images (and neutral images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (ACS vs INS; OCD-related vs neutral) and whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses with Talairach coordinates; the sample (OCD patients) is eligible. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because the emotional stimuli were self-generated autobiographical memories (internally-generated imagery cued by brief phrases) rather than externally-presented VISUAL stimuli (e.g., pictures, film), and therefore does not meet inclusion criterion I7. The study does meet other criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed emotion regulation strategy — distancing/reappraisal), I8 (eligible participant groups including MDD and healthy controls), and I9 (within-task comparisons of regulation conditions and related analyses). However, it does not appear to report a group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation map with peak coordinates in standard space (I10 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

Full text is not provided in the materials supplied (only title, authors, abstract/metadata note that the preprint is available elsewhere). Cannot verify core methods/results. Specifically: inclusion criteria met: none can be confirmed. Inclusion criteria not met/cannot be verified: I5 (task-based fMRI) — title implies fMRI but methods not available to confirm task vs. resting/state; I6 (instructed emotion regulation strategy) — not described in supplied text; I7 (visual emotional stimuli) — not described; I8 (sample reporting/group separation) — not described; I9 (within-task contrasts reported) — not described; I10/I11 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps with coordinates or tables/figures) — not available. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) can be confirmed from the incomplete content. Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot apply the review inclusion criteria; per instructions I exclude this record pending retrieval of the full article.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation with whole-brain analyses in adolescents with ASD, but the in-scanner task is neurofeedback/SCP self-regulation using neutral visual cues (triangles) rather than instructed emotion regulation of emotional visual stimuli. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample qualifies), I10 (whole-brain, voxelwise task maps reported), I11 (results clearly described). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal; participants were instructed to apply neurofeedback regulation strategies, not to regulate emotional responses), I7 (stimuli are neutral geometric cues, not emotional visual stimuli), I9 (within-task contrasts reported are Up vs Down SCP regulation, not contrasts of emotion regulation vs view). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are expressly triggered. Therefore the study does not address the meta-analysis objective and must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a free-viewing movie task (visual film clips) with group-level analyses comparing responses to positive, negative, and neutral stimuli. The authors modeled each trial with a GLM to produce whole-brain, voxelwise parameter maps and report brain regions (AAL2 atlas intersections and supplementary tables/figures) that inform condition and age-group classification. The study therefore provides within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (processing of negative/positive/neutral stimuli) and reports whole-brain results described in text/tables/supplement. Participants include children and adults. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Based on these elements the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion requirements for unregulated visual-emotion viewing and whole-brain reporting.

This is a task-based fMRI study using dynamic visual facial stimuli and reports unregulated viewing contrasts (Emotion > Fixation). It includes adult clinical and control groups with separate group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported with peak coordinates (standard space/MNI). Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction was given, the review objective accepts unregulated viewing contrasts; the study therefore provides eligible within-task contrasts and whole-brain results relevant to the meta-analysis.
